articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race
Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang 's has global implications.

The 63-year-old is the leading face of the artificial intelligence revolution with his black leather jacket and fluff of grey hair. He runs the company Nvidia, which produces highly coveted computer chips. That's landed him on a late-night phone call with President Donald Trump , a promoter of the industry.

But Mr. Huang was also liaising with a Chinese businesswoman who has allegedly fed intelligence — as well as advanced chips — to China. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed.

It's a saga of personal betrayal, corporate espionage and high-tech development, and the fallout is spreading across Washington. There are bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill. The U.S. Department of Justice has opened its own probe. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, is conducting an internal review.

Some expect the technology to reshape human civilisation by imbuing computers with the vast powers of creation and analysis, and Mr. Trump has repeated that “whoever wins AI, wins." Nvidia is the backbone of America's plans for dominating the field.
When asked about Mr. Huang's affair, Mr. Trump said this week that he had spoken to the tech executive as the scandal grew.
“I think he'll be in good shape," President Trump said, adding that "he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
As for when the President first learned about the concerns involving Ms. Alice Huang, Mr. Trump brushed off the question.
“They could have been mentioned," he said. "Certainly it didn't make much of an impact on me.”
With the AI race between the U.S. and China often framed as a fierce and consequential rivalry , the Justice Department has persistently warned of the espionage threat posed by Beijing.
That includes efforts to cultivate well-placed relationships in government and private industry, as well as to acquire sensitive technology, such as U.S.-developed AI chips.

Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the U.S. Commerce Department over allegations that it skirted U.S. export laws and routed a large number of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese users. The company denied those allegations. U.S. intelligence officials eventually concluded that Ms. Alice Huang had spied for China, according to The New York Times.

articles.title: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries

An agenda item on the Himalayas proposed by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan has not been included in the formal list of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) after failing to secure the backing of the developed nations.
The COP 31 commenced on Monday (November 9, 2026) in Antalya, Turkiye. Agenda items refer to the list of topics that are formally taken up for discussion at the conference every year.

Speaking to PTI at COP31, Shisir Khanal, Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries.
He said some nations explicitly backed the proposal raised on Monday (November 9, 2026), while others remained reluctant.

“This is part of a big negotiation. Different major blocs did not support it, and that made it difficult for the agenda to go through. From our side, we pushed as hard as we could. There were different voices in the room. Some explicitly supported our agenda, while others were quite reluctant,” he said.
A source with direct knowledge of the discussions said developed nations did not show interest when the three countries formally pushed the proposal.

“The agenda focused on the Himalayas was clearly diluted, and it was the European Union which did not show any interest in this agenda. Even though the issue is not completely off the charts, a high-level dialogue is expected on it soon,” the source told PTI on condition of anonymity.
The source added that developing nations did not object to or block the proposal when it was raised.

Asked which countries supported the proposal, Mr. Khanal said several Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and mountain nations were positive, while developed countries were reluctant to take up a new agenda.

According to the Nepal government, a research dialogue is expected during the upcoming sessions at COP31, and the presidency has assured that a final text addressing mountain-related issues will be included in the conference's outcome document.

“Compared to the past, we feel there is positive momentum, with the world community increasingly seeing the mountain issue as one of the core issues. That recognition is building. It may take some time to get where we really want to be, but we feel we are on a positive track,” Mr. Khanal said.

Asked why Nepal was emphasising the 1.5 degrees Celsius temperature overshoot in its proposal, Khanal said there was an urgent need to understand the consequences as global temperatures approach that threshold.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. articles.title: IT hubs see 82% commute by personal vehicles, just 2% use public transport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As Cyberabad grapples with growing traffic congestion, an overwhelming 82% of commuter movement across its key IT hubs is accounted for by personal vehicles, while public transport contributes just around 2%, highlighting the region’s dependence on private modes of transport.

According to data presented by Cyberabad Police and the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC), traffic across 15 key IT-sector locations exceeds 2.5 million vehicles and people every day. The figures underline the scale of the mobility challenge in one of Hyderabad’s fastest-growing employment hubs, which has a resident population of around 3.5 million spread across approximately 637 sq. km, apart from a substantial daily commuter population travelling from other parts of the city.

With around six lakh IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) employees represented by the corporates participating in a stakeholder interaction on Tuesday, Cyberabad Police are looking to bring companies on board to encourage a shift towards shared and sustainable commuting practices.

Director General of Police C.V. Anand stressed the need for public participation, corporate collaboration and sustained awareness campaigns to improve road discipline and traffic management. Highlighting the five pillars of traffic management, namely Education, Enforcement, Engineering, Emergency and Enablement, he said changing established commuting habits would require continuous outreach through schools, colleges, workplaces and local communities.

Cyberabad Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh and SCSC CEO Naved Alam Khan presented an overview of the traffic situation in Cyberabad and outlined the measures being undertaken to address congestion.

“In a first-of-its-kind initiative, we brought together real estate developers, including My Home Group, Google and other MNCs, urging them to take an active role in easing traffic congestion through measures such as staggered office timings, traffic management initiatives and greater participation in improving traffic flow,” said Mr Singh.

Officials also called upon companies to promote employee carpooling, increase the use of larger shared transport vehicles, introduce centralised shuttle services and synchronise hybrid work schedules. Improved parking management and incentives for employees using public transport were also highlighted as possible measures.

The authorities also unveiled the logo of ‘Cyberabad Moves’, a three-day exhibition and symposium scheduled to be held from November 26 to 28 at T-Hub. The event will bring together government departments, startups, civil society organisations, school students, corporate leaders and citizens to explore practical and technology-driven solutions to urban mobility challenges.

articles.title: World Wars and India’s sacrifice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: We owe it to ourselves to be honest with our past, just as we owe it to our armed forces to honour the sacrifices of those who went before them

On the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month, most Commonwealth and other allied nations fall silent for two minutes to honour the fallen of the two World Wars. Not so much in India: wreaths are laid in cantonments, but for most, this is just another day. India has an uneasy relationship with Remembrance Day. However, the idea that the World Wars were something that happened to someone else, somewhere else, could not be further from the truth.

Indian ambivalence over the two World Wars belies its enormous contribution to fighting fascism. Undivided (British) India sent 1.5 million men to fight in World War I, 74,000 of whom never returned home. For WWII, India produced the largest volunteer army of 2.5 million soldiers, with 87,00–89,000 making the ultimate sacrifice. The princely states also sent significant troops. Whereas the Indians who fought in the Great War were mostly sent to distant lands, in WWII, about 7,00,000 of them were defending Indian territory. The war came home to India when Japan invaded the country in March 1944.

articles.title: Civil police officer injured in attack by detained man in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The officer was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance in the city allegedly bit on his hands while he was being taken in a police vehicle for medical examination

A civil police officer (CPO) attached to the Ernakulam North police station was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance near the North overbridge bit on his hands when he was being taken in a police vehicle for medical examination, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

This comes two days after another CPO who was on traffic duty at the High Court bus stand was injured after a recklessly driven private bus rammed him. The incident occurred after the officer stopped a row of vehicles for an ambulance to pass through.

The Ernakulam Central police have registered a case against Muhammed Iqbal, 25, of Sashthamkotta in Kollam who, while being reportedly under the influence of intoxicants, bit on the hands of the police officer named Ajith Paul. He was seated on the last row of the police vehicle, from where he jumped into the middle row seat and reportedly tried to force open the door as the vehicle reached the Ernakulam General Hospital.

The officer was injured as he attempted to overpower him. The detainee also reportedly used abusive words. The police charged him under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Section 121 (1) — voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant to deter him from discharging his duty and 296(b) — use of obscene words in a public place.

He was taken for medical examination after he reportedly turned unruly at the police station soon after he was detained. He allegedly continued to create unruly scenes at the station even after being brought back after medical examination, a video of which went viral. Following these, he was remanded in judicial custody.

Archana Veeramani, 49, the daughter of R. Veeramani, being investigated as the main accused in a series of child sexual abuse cases, approached the Madras High Court with a plea to order an investigation into the human rights violations allegedly perpetrated against her by the State police and also to quash the summons issued after forcibly making her deboard a Singapore-bound airplane on October 23, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan is expected to hear her plea on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). The High Court Registry had numbered her writ petition (criminal) subject to maintainability. articles.title: Focus on Tamil during Kandasashthi: Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He urged temples under the purview of the department to ensure that Odhuvars chant/sing the Thirupugazh, Thirumurai, and Kandasashthi kavacham

Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) S. Ramesh on Tuesday said that Tamil language and literature will be given priority during the Kandasashthi festival in all major Murugan temples.

He urged temples under the purview of the department to ensure that Odhuvars chant/sing the Thirupugazh, Thirumurai, and Kandasashthi kavacham. Priests should also give priority to Tamil in all pujas and proceedings during the festival. Discourses and concerts should be in Tamil as well, he added.

In a set of directions issued to executive officers of temples, the Minister said that special arrangements must be made for persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and mothers-to-be at temples for darshan. Volunteers should be made available to assist such devotees, said an official statement here.

Mr. Ramesh said that temple officials should coordinate with the police, fire and other departments to ensure proper arrangements such as drinking water, toilets and medical care for devotees for darshan, during Kandasashthi and Sura Samharam.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu police step-up surveillance on habitual offenders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 443 accused persons arrested in Statewide drive against rowdyism
The Tamil Nadu police have arrested 443 accused persons involved in various crimes, including drug offences and violent crimes, across the State and enhanced vigil on habitual offenders.

In a two-day operation against rowdyism and organised crime, which was launched on Monday, the police conducted intensive checks at places frequented by persons with criminal antecedents. Police personnel checked the activities of more than 15,000 anti-social elements and thousands of vehicles as part of the operation, which resulted in the arrest of 443 suspects who were produced in local courts and remanded in judicial custody.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Director-General of Police and Head of the Police Force, Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, said the two-day operation was planned decisively to curb criminal activities, disrupt drug distribution networks, and reinforce absolute public order.

Police teams across Tamil Nadu systematically tracked and checked 8,626 listed rowdies. As many as 796 habitual offenders were placed under strict preventive surveillance. During the drive, 1,624 drug offenders were tracked and checked. 77 individuals actively involved in illicit drug sale were taken into custody.

To prevent retaliatory crimes and maintain public peace, Dr Aggarwal said the police stepped up surveillance on 2,924 accused individuals previously involved in murder and assault cases, including those recently released from prison. “This proactive supervision led to the registration of 163 fresh cases and the arrest of 167 violent offenders,” the DGP said.

He said drone patrolling was conducted to ensure the safety of residential neighbourhoods and commercial areas. The state police used drones effectively and clamped down on open-air public nuisance. The police also tracked and checked the activities of 1,057 criminals belonging to deep-rooted criminal syndicates.

Resolving long-standing judicial bottlenecks, law-enforcement teams successfully tracked down and executed 73 Non-Bailable Warrants (NBWs) against fleeing or non-compliant offenders during the two-day operation.

“The Tamil Nadu Police reiterates its uncompromising commitment to maintaining absolute Law and Order, ensuring community tranquillity, and protecting the citizens of the State. Strict, proactive surprise operations of this scale will continue to be deployed against any elements attempting to disrupt public peace,” Dr Aggarwal said.

articles.title: 10 years since demonetisation: Cash usage unchanged, fake notes on the rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: This Deepavali marks 10 years since Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced overnight demonetisation of 86% of the country’s cash. Data shows some stated aims of the move remain largely unmet

Ten years after demonetisation , Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data show that the exercise has had little impact on reducing cash in circulation and that detection of counterfeit notes, particularly ₹500 notes, has also increased.
On the other hand, the value of transactions on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has grown steadily year after year, even when measured as a percentage of India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.summary: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently
articles.keyPoints:
• Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently
• If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.
• In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Vaiko releases 34-year crime report; rebukes allies for criticising T.N. government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid ongoing accusations by Opposition parties of increase in crime and deteriorating law and order in Tamil Nadu, MDMK general secretary Vaiko on Tuesday released a catalogue of crimes that occurred over the past 34 years. He also lamented that the TVK-led government was being criticised by two of its coalition partners.
Addressing journalists in Chennai on Tuesday, he said except the IUML and the MDMK, the other parties within the ruling alliance have been criticising the administration.

Mr. Vaiko released a list detailing crimes committed in the State between May 1991 and May 2026. Citing the list compiled by the Madurai-based human rights organisation People’s Watch, he highlighted several major criminal incidents.

Speaking on the subject for over an hour, Vaiko also recounted the backdrop of key moments from his own political journey during this period. In particular, he detailed the circumstances surrounding his arrest under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA) in July 2002. He noted that upon learning of the Tamil Nadu government’s decision to detain him under POTA, he advanced his return from the United States — originally scheduled for July 15 — and arrived in Chennai on July 11 to court arrest. He added while he was meant to be lodged in the Vellore Central Prison, authorities attempted to detain him at the Madurai Central Prison en route, an effort that was abandoned only after his fierce resistance.

He also recalled that it was former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi who first addressed him as “Vaiko” instead of his full name V. Gopalasamy. He recounted that during the inaugural meeting held in Delhi to form the National Front, M. Karunanidhi had sent him a note on a slip of paper addressed to ‘ Thambi Vaikovukku’ .

Mr. Vaiko alleged some time after he founded the MDMK, L. Ganesan and Gingee N. Ramachandran attempted to split the party and organise a rival general council meeting on the instructions of the DMK leadership, but those efforts ended in failure.

He further recalled that following his release from prison under POTA, he undertook a padayatra from Tirunelveli to Chennai alongside 1,200 people, demanding an end to caste and communal clashes and the complete eradication of narcotics. Although he was denied entry into Chennai as the march neared the city, he defied the restrictions, entered Chennai, and addressed a public meeting.

Mr. Vaiko also mentioned that when Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa as a special guest to his swearing-in ceremony, he vehemently opposed the move and was arrested after staging a demonstration at Jantar Mantar.

Stating he had opposed the Sterlite plant in Thoothukudi from the very beginning, Mr. Vaiko alleged fresh efforts were under way to reopen the facility under the pretext of producing “Green Copper.” He claimed Vedanta’s Anil Agarwal had sought an appointment with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for this purpose; however, following his own appeal urging the Chief Minister not to meet him, the meeting did not take place, and Mr. Agarwal has now approached the court.
Prior to Mr. Vaiko’s address, leaders from his party spoke in detail about his political contributions.

articles.title: Strategic autonomy must guide India’s Starlink policy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India must balance Starlink’s benefits with national security and strategic autonomy

Recently, Elon Musk unleashed a volley of social media posts, accusing Indian “oligarchs” of impeding Starlink’s entry into India. The government rejected the accusation and clarified that all satellite operators must go through the same regulatory process. The ensuing public debate has centred on Mr. Musk, Mukesh Ambani, protectionism and telecom competition. All this obscures important questions of how much control India will have over Starlink once it operates here.

In its current form, Starlink is unlikely to replace fibre and mobile networks because they have almost opposite strengths. Fibre and mobile networks take time and money to set up, but can serve many people in one area. Starlink reaches remote places without towers or cables but is limited by how many users it can serve in one region. While fibre and mobile networks are optimised for density, Starlink is optimised for reach. Starlink has previously stopped taking new residential customers in areas where it ran out of capacity.

articles.title: Karnataka-registered doctors may be allowed to practise in Kasaragod: Keralam Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Keralam government has recommended to the State Medical Council that doctors registered with the Karnataka Medical Council be allowed to practise in Kasaragod, considering the district’s special circumstances, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said.
The medical council is expected to take a favourable decision on the recommendation soon, the Minister said while inaugurating ‘Kayakalpam’, a public outreach programme of the Health Minister.

Government hospitals should have adequate number of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory technicians, the Minister said, adding that additional posts had been sought. Their early sanction would considerably ease staff shortage in the district.
The extension of the tenure of National Health Mission employees in Kasaragod till March 31 was also an indication of the government’s commitment to the district, he said.

The Minister said that he would direct the authorities to convene a meeting of the Endosulfan cell soon. Periye in Kasaragod was among the four locations proposed by the government to the Centre for setting up an All India Institute of Medical Sciences, he said.

Instructions had been issued to make hostel facilities available at the Kasaragod Medical College within two months. The construction of a hostel for nursing students would begin within three months, he added.
The government would ensure the services of a forensic surgeon at the Kanhangad district hospital. A new building for the District Medical Office would be constructed at a cost of ₹4.8 crore.

articles.title: Keralam power purchase row: CM Satheesan plays down issue, dismisses charges that Electricity Minister was kept in the dark
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Satheesan says KSEB had 'never entered into a power purchase agreement with GNA in the first place’ and that he is ‘not aware whether KSEB had misled him or not’

Amid a raging controversy over a power purchase proposal via over-the-counter (OTC) platform GNA Energy, Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) sought to play it down, saying the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) had “never entered into a power purchase agreement (PPA) with GNA in the first place.” The Chief Minister also dismissed the charge that Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph was kept in the dark about the developments as “baseless.”
At a post-Cabinet press briefing in Thiruvananthapuram, Mr. Satheesan said he was “not aware whether the KSEB had misled him or not” on the power situation.

However, an October 29 note the then KSEB chairman and managing director M.G. Rajamanickam sent to the government through the Electricity Minister seeking a quick decision on the power purchase options from GNA Energy and the Himachal Pradesh government did have a sentence saying Keralam could “face prolonged power cuts,” he said. “Any Chief Minister would have been scared of being held responsible for causing power cuts by sitting on a file,” Mr. Satheesan said. However, the Chief Minister remained noncommittal on whether an investigation would be ordered into the KSEB report.

On Mr. Sunny Joseph’s statement that he got to know about the government decision not to proceed with the ‘GNA agreement’ from media reports, the Chief Minister said it “was so since no agreement was in fact signed” with GNA Energy.
“The file was forwarded to me by the Minister himself. The KSEB sent it to him and he forwarded it to me. I will return it to him, and from him, it will go to KSEB. Everything is pucca,” he said.

According to the Chief Minister, the file mentioned two options – a supply offer from Himachal Pradesh at ₹14.50 per unit and another from GNA at ₹8.63 and 8.90 per unit. GNA was seen as the better option as the price was lower. Meanwhile, the quantum offered by the latter was sold to Rajasthan at ₹15.50. But an examination of the power situation revealed that Keralam faced no shortage in November and December, but may require it later on.

On Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan’s demand for a judicial probe into the power purchase proposal, Mr. Satheesan said Mr. Vijayan “keeps contradicting himself.” CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan, Mr. Satheesan said, was “clueless” about the power purchase proposal. The absence of planning and long-term power purchase agreements during the tenure of the CPI(M)-led LDF government had led to the recent power crisis, he said. “I would call it criminal negligence,” he said, adding that only 300 MW was additionally generated during the 10-year LDF rule. Despite an increase in the number of rooftop solar units, no storage systems were installed, he added.

Mr. Satheesan said the government would purchase electricity at the lowest available price. As part of addressing the energy needs of the State in the long run, the government intended to step up renewable energy generation with battery storage, he said, adding that a decision would be taken on long-term power purchase agreements this month (November) itself.
Also, the government intended to announce and implement projects with regard to the State’s emerging electricity needs in another five years, he said.

articles.title: No discrepancy in votes polled and counted in Mumbai North LS polls: EC officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electors are those who are on electoral rolls and voters are those who actually caste votes, they noted

Election Commission officials on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) rejected media reports claiming discrepancy in the number of votes counted and polled in the Mumbai North seat during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, saying the reports confused between electors and voters.
Electors are those who are on electoral rolls and voters are those who actually caste votes, they noted.
Citing the index card, they said Mumbai North had a total of 18,12,115 registered electors, comprising 9,69,143 men, 8,42,559 women and 413 third-gender persons.
Of these, 10,33,267 voters (60.44%) exercised their franchise in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, including 5,60,391 men, 4,72,815 women and 61 third-gender voters.
The officials said the index card is the sole official document about voters and voting, which is available on the poll panel’s website.
BJP leader and Union minister Piyush Goyal won the Mumbai North seat in 2024.

articles.title: Keralam child rights panel registers case over alleged assault by Anganwadi worker on 3-year-old
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the child’s parent’s complaint, the worker allegedly struck the child on his hand and severely pinched his ears after he accidentally urinated in his pants

The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a case following a complaint that an Anganwadi worker physically assaulted a three-year-old child at Anganwadi No. 98 in Kulamada, Kollam.

According to the child’s parent’s complaint, the worker allegedly struck the child on his hand and severely pinched his ears after he accidentally urinated in his pants. The parent reported that the child remains under severe emotional distress due to the incident, adding that similar complaints had previously been raised against the same worker. Crucial evidence, including hospital records, a detailed medical report from the examining doctor, and photographs documenting the child’s injuries, was submitted alongside the formal complaint.

Taking serious note of the incident, the child rights panel has sought detailed reports and explanations from key officials, including the District Police Chief (Kollam City), Parippally Station House Officer (SHO) and the District Child Protection Officer.

fullParagraphs: On Chennai recording higher pollution levels this Deepavali, the Minister said the government would take up targeted awareness campaigns in Valasaravakkam, where the air quality levels were the highest in the city on Deepavali

The Tamil Nadu government will convene a meeting with firecracker manufacturers and industry associations in Sivakasi towards the end of November to encourage the production of green crackers, Environment Minister V.K. Rajeev said in a press meet on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). The initiative is expected to reduce emissions from firecrackers by 30%, he said.

On Chennai recording higher pollution levels this Deepavali, the Minister said the government would take up targeted awareness campaigns in Valasaravakkam, where the air quality levels were the highest in the city on Deepavali for the third consecutive year. The government would also encourage tree planting in the locality, he said.
As announced in the Assembly, monitoring stations would be installed at 80 locations, for which a Government Order would be issued shortly, he said.

On air pollution levels exceeding an AQI of 1,000 in some areas, Dr. Rajeev said the TNPCB reported daily average readings, unlike private monitoring platforms that provided hourly data. He said pollution peaked between 8 p.m. and 11 p.m. as people burst crackers simultaneously at night, but the levels declined after 11 p.m.

Towards the end of November, the government would convene a meeting with firecracker manufacturers and industry associations in Sivakasi to discuss their production, he said, adding that several companies had already cooperated with the initiative and increased production of green crackers.

Referring to the air quality readings recorded after Deepavali, the Minister said that weaker wind flow during the monsoon could affect the dispersal of pollutants. He added that a significant number of vehicles come onto the roads after festival celebrations end, which can add to the pollution levels.

Dismissing allegations by AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on the closure of over 450 industrial units resulting in job losses, Dr. Rajeev said the TNPCB had ordered the closure of only 171 units, which included 133 through the Board and 38 through district administrations.

“These units are in his home district. His anger stems from the fact that factories belonging to his associates are now facing scrutiny, unlike during his tenure when no action was taken against them. We cannot remain inactive. Any industry that harms the public or damages the environment will face immediate action,” he said.

articles.title: U.S. and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Scott Bessent
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity”

The United States and ‌China should harbor no illusions about their differences on artificial intelligence as they navigate cooperation to ​mitigate the technology’s risks while competing for Artificial Intelligence (AI) supremacy, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said ⁠on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

Mr. Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said in prepared remarks to the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations in New York that he wanted to “build ‌a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity.”

The meeting in Shenzhen, to be held on the sidelines of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders summit, will advance a new bilateral ‌dialogue on “superintelligence”, or SI, Bessent said, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology.
The dialogue is meant ‌to ⁠guard against shared risks and “prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems,” Bessent said.

“We also expect ⁠to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said, adding the two sides had agreed to establish a direct channel for alerting each other to serious incidents.

Mr. Trump and /Mr. ​Xi agreed on the new AI alert ‌system during their previous meeting at the White House in September, but Trump at the time also said he was reluctant to add new guardrails because he wanted to preserve US leadership.

“As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management — and to demonstrate how two nations ‌can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership,” Mr. Bessent said.

“As we do so, we ​should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China. As I stated earlier, our interests will not always coincide. And our approach to every challenge, likewise, will ⁠not always converge,” he added.

Mr. Bessent’s remarks made no mention of the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , who is facing an investigation by the AI chipmaker’s board after a New York Times report that he had an affair ‌with a businesswoman suspected by U.S. security services of being a Chinese intelligence asset.
China’s Foreign Ministry has called the spying accusations “groundless” and “a smear.”

N vidia has said its board has no reason to believe U.S. national security or company secrets were compromised and that Huang has committed to cooperating with the internal review. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife, but provided no details about the relationship.
While Mr. Huang was present at the Trump-Xi summits in Beijing in May and in Washington in September, it was unclear if Trump would bring him ‌to the APEC summit.

articles.title: Rubio says 'no need' to attack Iran as diplomacy gathers pace
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table

Top U.S. diplomat Marco Rubio said on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) that he saw no need to attack Iran again, as diplomatic efforts to end the war gathered steam and Tehran urged Washington to accept its demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Hours after President Donald Trump said he saw "positive momentum" towards resolving the eight-month war, Mr/ Rubio said the United States' squeezing of Iran's economy made further attacks unnecessary.

"The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations," the Secretary of State said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. "That's what I told our allies here today."

Iran's efforts to blockade Hormuz, the major exit route for Gulf energy shipments, have sent oil prices soaring — a major factor in the humbling of Mr. Trump's Republicans in last week's midterm elections.

Washington has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and in August announced what it called an "economic asphyxiation" campaign aimed at financially strangling Iran, already battered by years of sanctions.

Britain's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called for greater efforts to end the conflict, while warning of the economic damage of an ongoing impasse. "We need to move beyond the 'no war, no peace' stalemate, which is causing deep economic pain for our countries," he said in Paris.
"We must see an all-out diplomatic effort to end this conflict, prevent a nuclear Iran and the threats it poses around the world, and get the Strait of Hormuz properly reopened."

Washington has appeared to taper down its threats of renewed strikes after the Republicans' defeat, and even Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — who launched the war alongside Trump and recently lobbied to "forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran" — appeared to recognise the shifting diplomatic reality.

"In the very near future, we're going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us," he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table.

Iran's demands have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing its assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US blockade of its ports. "The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions," Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA news agency.

articles.title: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after GOP's midterm wipeout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: After Democrats trounced GOP and won control of the next Congress, Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party
It's business as usual for President Donald Trump's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armour blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighbourhood early Saturday (November 7, 2026). In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.
Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.
After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Mr. Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.
“I'd love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday (November 6, 2026).

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mr. Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”
María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.
“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Ms. Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as in places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.
Erick Gasca, 31, got home Friday night (November 6, 2026) after an evening playing board games with friends. He lives near Adventist Health White Memorial Medical Center in Los Angeles.
An “unprecedented” number of vehicles with tinted windows and no license plates were parked near the hospital's emergency room entrance, he said.

It's business as usual for President Donald Trump's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armour blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighbourhood early Saturday (November 7, 2026). In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.

Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.

After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Mr. Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.

“I'd love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday (November 6, 2026).

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mr. Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”

María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.

“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Ms. Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as in places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.

Erick Gasca, 31, got home Friday night (November 6, 2026) after an evening playing board games with friends. He lives near Adventist Health White Memorial Medical Center in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries

An agenda item on the Himalayas proposed by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan has not been included in the formal list of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) after failing to secure the backing of the developed nations.
The COP 31 commenced on Monday (November 9, 2026) in Antalya, Turkiye. Agenda items refer to the list of topics that are formally taken up for discussion at the conference every year.

Speaking to PTI at COP31, Shisir Khanal, Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries.
He said some nations explicitly backed the proposal raised on Monday (November 9, 2026), while others remained reluctant.

“This is part of a big negotiation. Different major blocs did not support it, and that made it difficult for the agenda to go through. From our side, we pushed as hard as we could. There were different voices in the room. Some explicitly supported our agenda, while others were quite reluctant,” he said.
A source with direct knowledge of the discussions said developed nations did not show interest when the three countries formally pushed the proposal.

“The agenda focused on the Himalayas was clearly diluted, and it was the European Union which did not show any interest in this agenda. Even though the issue is not completely off the charts, a high-level dialogue is expected on it soon,” the source told PTI on condition of anonymity.
The source added that developing nations did not object to or block the proposal when it was raised.

Asked which countries supported the proposal, Mr. Khanal said several Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and mountain nations were positive, while developed countries were reluctant to take up a new agenda.

According to the Nepal government, a research dialogue is expected during the upcoming sessions at COP31, and the presidency has assured that a final text addressing mountain-related issues will be included in the conference's outcome document.

“Compared to the past, we feel there is positive momentum, with the world community increasingly seeing the mountain issue as one of the core issues. That recognition is building. It may take some time to get where we really want to be, but we feel we are on a positive track,” Mr. Khanal said.

Asked why Nepal was emphasising the 1.5 degrees Celsius temperature overshoot in its proposal, Khanal said there was an urgent need to understand the consequences as global temperatures approach that threshold.

articles.title: India’s efforts to clean its air need not slow its economic growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The best interventions must address air pollution while supporting development priorities. Cleaner industrial processes may reduce emissions while improving efficiency. Clean cooking can reduce household smoke while improving convenience and health. Better waste management can reduce open burning while improving urban services

India ranked 176 out of 177 countries in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI), which is published by the Yale and Columbia Universities in the U.S. The index assesses 47 indicators across 12 issue categories. Of them, India performed the worst on air quality, where it ranked 175, yet it did considerably better on air pollution, ranking 88. This contrast is illustrative: doing better at controlling select emissions does not necessarily mean the air people breathe gets better. And only the latter matters for India’s health burden.

The State of Global Air 2025 report estimated that more than 20 lakh deaths in India in 2023 could be attributed to air pollution. A Central Pollution Control Board assessment in 2012 also found lower lung function in 43.5% of Delhi schoolchildren compared to 25.7% of children in a control group.

articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race
Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang 's has global implications.

The 63-year-old is the leading face of the artificial intelligence revolution with his black leather jacket and fluff of grey hair. He runs the company Nvidia, which produces highly coveted computer chips. That's landed him on a late-night phone call with President Donald Trump , a promoter of the industry.

But Mr. Huang was also liaising with a Chinese businesswoman who has allegedly fed intelligence — as well as advanced chips — to China. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed.

It's a saga of personal betrayal, corporate espionage and high-tech development, and the fallout is spreading across Washington. There are bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill. The U.S. Department of Justice has opened its own probe. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, is conducting an internal review.

Some expect the technology to reshape human civilisation by imbuing computers with the vast powers of creation and analysis, and Mr. Trump has repeated that “whoever wins AI, wins." Nvidia is the backbone of America's plans for dominating the field.
When asked about Mr. Huang's affair, Mr. Trump said this week that he had spoken to the tech executive as the scandal grew.
“I think he'll be in good shape," President Trump said, adding that "he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
As for when the President first learned about the concerns involving Ms. Alice Huang, Mr. Trump brushed off the question.
“They could have been mentioned," he said. "Certainly it didn't make much of an impact on me.”
With the AI race between the U.S. and China often framed as a fierce and consequential rivalry, the Justice Department has persistently warned of the espionage threat posed by Beijing.
That includes efforts to cultivate well-placed relationships in government and private industry, as well as to acquire sensitive technology, such as U.S.-developed AI chips.

Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the U.S. Commerce Department over allegations that it skirted U.S. export laws and routed a large number of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese users. The company denied those allegations. U.S. intelligence officials eventually concluded that Ms. Alice Huang had spied for China, according to The New York Times.

articles.title: What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. articles.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers

Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, in a listing that could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion.
The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers and is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.

The maker of the Claude AI models said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. The shares will trade under the ticker "ANT."
Seven tech companies including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft have also agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement, the filing showed.
The companies are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power.
Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would have made it the largest IPO on record.
Even at the top of its price range, the offering would fall short of the record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which raised $86 billion in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.
Anthropic has been aiming to go public the week of November 16, and reports said its shares would begin trading on November 19.

Anthropic's listing is "just another chapter" in investors' worries over the cost of the AI buildout and how it gets financed, Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management, told AFP.

"But at the end of the day, I think there are three massive companies that investors have wanted to be part of for the last three years and that's SpaceX for sure, Anthropic is next, and perhaps next year OpenAI," he said.

The listing comes as Wall Street digests the results of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats, who are more wary of AI, won control of both chambers of Congress and have vowed to put the brakes on President Donald Trump's agenda.
The slide has brought volatility to shares of companies linked to the AI boom, with AI chip-maker Nvidia particularly in focus after chief executive Jensen Huang was caught up in a spy scandal.

articles.title: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation

Revelations that Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen ​Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker’s board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for ‌the company and concerns about the board’s ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, “There have definitely been affair scandals and ​sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No,” said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

Lipton was using a ⁠term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation “regarding the national security concerns raised ‌in news reports,” according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company’s code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal “with ‌or without cause” by the vote of a majority of directors.
The company’s advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI ‌superiority. ⁠China’s Foreign Ministry called the spying claim “a groundless accusation, slander and a smear.”
Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as ⁠close ties to Trump. Huang owns 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.
Shares in Nvidia were down 6% on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang’s affair.

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three ​independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark ‌Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.
The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple’s Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.
But the US probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside Huang for decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct.

“If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street ‌as well as in Silicon Valley would say they’re entitled to some leeway or deference,” said Marc Goldstein, head of US research for ​proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.

articles.title: Firecrackers still Delhi’s top pollutant after Deepavali, IITM finds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on November 9, a day after Deepavali, before declining on November 11, the IITM models showed

Firecrackers emerged as the biggest contributor to Delhi's air pollution on both Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10), accounting for 71.1% and 29.8% of the pollution load, respectively, according to source-apportionment estimates by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM).

The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on Monday (November 9), a day after Deepavali, before declining on Tuesday (November 11), the IITM models showed.

The estimates had a standard deviation (SD) of 104.1 percentage points on Monday (November 9) and 27.7 percentage points on Tuesday (November 10), indicating considerable variability and uncertainty in the modelled contributions.

On Monday (November 9), vehicular emissions accounted for 6.9% of the pollution, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols at 5% and secondary organic aerosols at 4.5%. Mixed or unresolved biofuel contributed 4.45%, while mineral dust and ash and mixed combustion accounted for 2.5% each.

Wood burning contributed 1.3%, while waste burning, including municipal and plastic-rubber-containing waste, accounted for 1.1%. Coal combustion and industrial emissions contributed 0.5% and 0.2%, respectively.
On Tuesday (November 10), the contribution of firecrackers dropped to 29.8%, while secondary organic aerosols emerged as the second-largest contributor at 17.5%.
Vehicular emissions and secondary inorganic aerosols each accounted for 11.7% of the pollution load, while wood burning contributed 10.7% and waste burning 7.7%.
Vehicular emissions emerged as the third largest contributor to pollution on Tuesday (November 10).
Mixed combustion accounted for 5.1%, followed by mixed or unresolved biofuel at 3.3% and mineral dust and ash at 1.5%.
Delhi's average 24-hour Air Quality Index (AQI) had improved marginally to the 'poor' category on Tuesday (November 10), with the 4 p.m. reading settling at 299.
However, air quality deteriorated again on Wednesday (November 11), with the AQI climbing to 312, placing it in the 'very poor' category.
An AQI between 201 and 300 is classified as 'poor', while readings between 301 and 400 fall in the 'very poor' category.

articles.title: Over eight lakh glass bangles adorn Goddess Kanaka Durga for ‘Gajula Alankaram’ in Vijayawada
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The temple doubles the number of bangles used last year to decorate the deity and its premises

Indrakeeladri, the abode of Goddess Kanaka Durga in Vijayawada , came alive with ‘Gajula Alankaram’ (bangle decoration) of Goddess Kanaka Durga on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), on the auspicious occasion of ‘Kartika Shuddha Vidiya’ , observed as ‘Bhagini Hasta Bhojanam’ .

Over eight lakh colourful glass bangles were used to adorn the presiding deity and decorate the premises of the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam, including the sanctum sanctorum, corridors, ceilings and sub-shrines. The bangles, in vibrant shades of green, red, yellow and blue, were intricately arranged into garlands and decorative patterns.

Goddess Kanaka Durga adorned with glass bangles for Gajula Alankaram on Indrakeeladri in Vijayawada on Wednesday. Over eight lakh bangles decorated the deity and the temple, double last year's number. Photos: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/rv91oEsxb0

Temple Executive Officer V.K. Seena Naik said all arrangements had been completed in accordance with temple traditions and customs. Inspecting the arrangements on the sixth floor of the Maha Mantapam, he said the temple had used over four lakh bangles last year, while their number had been doubled this year to decorate both the main deity and the temple premises.
He said devotees and donors had contributed bangles in large quantities, with the temple administration making additional arrangements to meet the requirement.

Women devotees from different parts of the State thronged the temple to have darshan of the Goddess in the special alankaram. Following the rituals, the bangles worshipped in the presence of the deity were distributed to women devotees as prasadam.
