articles.title: Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: India is ready to mediate to establish grain safety agreement for “food corridors”, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy

India is ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish “food corridors”, announced Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcoming the offer after a telephone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of the Ukraine-Russia peace talks set to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Mr. Modi conveyed India’s “readiness” to help with all initiatives to end the nearly five-year-old conflict. The call was followed by another call between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump’s negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, will restart negotiations after three months with Russian and Ukrainian representatives to discuss security guarantees required for a possible ceasefire. The calls from New Delhi came just ahead of the talks in the UAE, and a week before Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the ASEAN-linked summits in Manila. Later this month, Mr. Trump is expected to travel to Shenzhen for the APEC summit in China, that Russian President Vladimir Putin is also expected to attend, making the timing of the Modi-Zelenskyy and Jaishankar-Lavrov calls more significant.

“Prime Minister [Modi] reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy,” the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement about the Modi-Zelenskyy call. “He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict,” it added.

In a post on social media, Mr. Zelenskyy said he had briefed Mr. Modi on the latest developments and stressed that Mr. Modi had said to Mr. Putin that the war must end. The Ukrainian President said Russia must understand that the “global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes” in the Black Sea, and called for India to clarify its peace proposal.

“It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end. Food security could be one such area. We discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” Mr. Zelenskyy wrote.

Within a couple of hours of the announcement, Mr. Jaishankar posted that he had spoken to his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov as well, and said their conversation had “focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives”. Mr. Jaishankar, who has been discussing India’s proposals on a grain export agreement or a food corridor in the Black Sea, on the safety of sea mariners, and safe passage for energy shipments with both countries, had first disclosed the initiatives during a visit to Poland and Ukraine in September. On October 22, during the visit of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to Delhi, Indian officials had said it had reached out to both Russian and Ukrainian governments with a “four-point proposal” for an agreement that would stop attacks on civilians, allow grain and energy exports from both countries through the Black Sea, and end the targeting of ships and seafarers, many of whom are Indian nationals. Highly placed officials had told The Hindu that New Delhi was in close contact with both sides over the specific proposal, and the government had hoped to hear back from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides at the earliest. With talks set to begin on Tuesday, it remains to be seen whether India will join the dialogue already in play with the U.S. and the UAE, or whether New Delhi plans a larger role in mediating or hosting talks between Russia and Ukraine in the future.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India is ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish “food corridors”, announced Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcoming the offer after a telephone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of the Ukraine-Russia peace talks set to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Mr. Modi conveyed India’s “readiness” to help with all initiatives to end the nearly five-year-old conflict. The call was followed by another call between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Within a couple of hours of the announcement, Mr. Jaishankar posted that he had spoken to his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov as well, and said their conversation had “focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives”. Mr. Jaishankar, who has been discussing India’s proposals on a grain export agreement or a food corridor in the Black Sea, on the safety of sea mariners, and safe passage for energy shipments with both countries, had first disclosed the initiatives during a visit to Poland and Ukraine in September. On October 22, during the visit of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to Delhi, Indian officials had said it had reached out to both Russian and Ukrainian governments with a “four-point proposal” for an agreement that would stop attacks on civilians, allow grain and energy exports from both countries through the Black Sea, and end the targeting of ships and seafarers, many of whom are Indian nationals. Highly placed officials had told The Hindu that New Delhi was in close contact with both sides over the specific proposal, and the government had hoped to hear back from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides at the earliest. With talks set to begin on Tuesday, it remains to be seen whether India will join the dialogue already in play with the U.S. and the UAE, or whether New Delhi plans a larger role in mediating or hosting talks between Russia and Ukraine in the future.

articles.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The deceased were identified as a staff nurse and four inmates of a government-recognised children’s home for girls
A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area.

On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned.

Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered.

Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way.

articles.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab.

Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity.
The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1.
Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts.

A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said.
The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone.

In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said.
The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department.
He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue and relief operations during the cyclone.

articles.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led government enjoys public goodwill despite concerns about it being directionless
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an ‘empty coffer,’ the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures

The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government, which completed six months in office on Monday (November 9, 2026), appears to be largely enjoying the goodwill of people, even though concerns are being raised about the regime’s tendency to be directionless.

Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an “empty coffer,” the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures. The “precarious” financial condition did not come in the way of his government carrying out some other steps such as the extension of the breakfast scheme for school students, the provision of gold rings to babies born at government hospitals, the distribution of eight-gram gold coins and silk saris to eligible women, and the expansion of free travel for women on buses of the State Transport Corporations.

Reports of a “marked reduction“ in corruption regarding government appointments, transfers, and public services have impressed many observers including former Union Minister P. Chidambaram and UN diplomat-turned-political writer R. Kannan. In an interview with this newspaper a couple of months ago, Mr. Chidambaram stated: “I also understand that sanctions for the appointment of teachers in [government-aided] schools and colleges have been sent by post.” According to Mr. Kannan, “transparency remains the Vijay administration’s strongest asset.” The ruling party’s national spokesperson, Americai V. Narayanan, says: “He [Mr. Vijay] does not do things to please others or earn applause. He does them because he genuinely believes in them. In politics, where symbolism often outweighs conviction, that distinction matters.”

Notwithstanding the general perception about the government‘s integrity, the two Dravidian majors — the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) — have been unsparing. One of the areas of their attack is on the power front, where the current regime had, ironically, begun with the increase in the quantum of free power to 200 units bimonthly to domestic consumers subject to the overall consumption not exceeding 500 units. The regime’s plans for power purchase on a short-term basis at a higher cost has raised questions about the government’s competence.

DMK president M.K. Stalin and AIADMK’s Amma Peravai secretary R.B. Udhayakumar wondered when Keralam could buy electricity at lower price, why Tamil Nadu has not been able to procure at comparable rates. Besides, even the lower price has triggered a controversy in the neighbouring State.

It is not only on the power front where the government is found on a weak wicket but also on many other policy matters. On the issue of wooing industrial investment, the Opposition’s attack has not been firmly rebutted by the government. As for the TVK regime’s project of building a new Secretariat complex, there has not been any categorical statement from the Chief Minister on the controversy triggered by it, though his Ministerial colleagues, at times, make different observations.

“The new government often appears directionless, evidenced by hasty decision-making and conspicuous silence on controversial issues,“ Mr. Kannan observes. He adds that moving forward, the priority must shift from perpetual campaigning to effective governance.

A senior citizen, who calls himself a “well wisher“ of the ruling party, points out that “a structured, periodic forum for district and block-level leaders would help. Without it, the party could pay a price in the forthcoming local body elections.”

Even as the TVK government faces a host of challenges in sustained governance, it is also expected to fulfil its key electoral promises such as the increase in the monthly assistance for women to ₹2,500.

articles.title: Man kills 4-year-old to sell his organs after watching video on making money quickly
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 27-year-old Basudev Korwa from Chhattisgarh is accused of having murdered his cousin’s son and extracting the boy’s organs, which he allegedly kept in a plastic bag

A 27-year-old man was arrested in Chhattisgarh’s Jashpur for allegedly killing a four-year-old boy, a relative of his, with the intention to sell the boy’s organs, the police said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
According to the police, the man, who works as an agricultural labourer, got the idea after watching a video that purportedly suggested organ sale as a way to make money quickly.

The accused, Basudev Korwa, alias Tangnu, lives in Sanna village. Basudev’s cousin, Ramjeet Ram, 36, also lives there with his wife and their children. On November 5, after getting Ramjeet Ram inebriated, Basudev allegedly lured one of his sons with chicken and fed him liquor. The accused is then alleged to have taken the boy to his hut, where he slit the child’s throat. According to the police, he then and removed the boy’s organs, including the kidneys.
Jashpur Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Lal Umed Singh said the accused buried the body at a different site after extracting the organs, which he kept in a plastic bag.

The following day, the boy’s father complained to the police about his son’s disappearance, and villagers mounted a search. The body, wrapped in a blanket, was discovered by a villager nearly 500 metres away from the field where both the victim and the accused lived in separate huts. A witness also told the police that the child had been seen with Basudev.
Upon his arrest, the police learnt that Basudev, who had received little formal education, had no understanding of how organ transplants worked and did not have a ready buyer.

Mr. Singh said that through the content the accused had consumed online, he was convinced that there would be a “buyer from Delhi” who would come and buy the organs he had supposedly “preserved” in the plastic bag.

Explaining the chain of events, the SSP said that Basudev, in a bid to make more money than the few hundred rupees he earned daily, had joined some groups on a chatting app that discussed ways to make money. However, all of the conversation was in English, which he did not understand.

“What came to his aid was an artificial intelligence [AI] assistant embedded in the chatting app that understood and replied in Hindi. As he started interacting with the app, it started redirecting him to other sites, which would open in the browser. One such video was about organ sales fetching good money,” said another senior police officer, adding that they were yet to find out the exact video that the accused watched because he does not have a registered profile on the streaming site and no saved browsing history.

Even as Basudev learned about the organ sale, he asked more questions to the AI assistant in the chat app, framing them in a manner that concealed his intent. "Yet the assistant issued warnings that organ sale was prohibited in India and that there were laws against it. Still, the accused went ahead with the plan. He chose the boy who called him ‘chachu [uncle]’ and trusted him,” said the officer.

The body, wrapped in a blanket, was discovered by a villager nearly 500 metres away from the field where both the victim and the accused lived in separate huts. A witness also told the police that the child had been seen with Basudev.

Upon his arrest, the police learnt that Basudev, who had received little formal education, had no understanding of how organ transplants worked and did not have a ready buyer.

Mr. Singh said that through the content the accused had consumed online, he was convinced that there would be a “buyer from Delhi” who would come and buy the organs he had supposedly “preserved” in the plastic bag.

Explaining the chain of events, the SSP said that Basudev, in a bid to make more money than the few hundred rupees he earned daily, had joined some groups on a chatting app that discussed ways to make money. However, all of the conversation was in English, which he did not understand.

“What came to his aid was an artificial intelligence [AI] assistant embedded in the chatting app that understood and replied in Hindi. As he started interacting with the app, it started redirecting him to other sites, which would open in the browser. One such video was about organ sales fetching good money,” said another senior police officer, adding that they were yet to find out the exact video that the accused watched because he does not have a registered profile on the streaming site and no saved browsing history.

Even as Basudev learned about the organ sale, he asked more questions to the AI assistant in the chat app, framing them in a manner that concealed his intent. "Yet the assistant issued warnings that organ sale was prohibited in India and that there were laws against it. Still, the accused went ahead with the plan. He chose the boy who called him ‘chachu [uncle]’ and trusted him,” said the officer.

articles.title: Tasmac’s Deepavali sales touch ₹441 crore amid POS machine glitches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore

The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) has recorded liquor sales worth ₹441.38 crore during Deepavali 2026. According to sources, on the eve of Deepavali, Tasmac sold liquor worth over ₹234.75 crore and on the day of the festival the sales stood at ₹206.63 crore.

Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore. Salem reported sales of ₹87.52 crore and Coimbatore at ₹70.66 crore. As Monday was a holiday, liquor sales are expected to remain at similar levels (sales of approximately ₹192 crore are expected).

Those tracking the liquor market in Tamil Nadu say sales have dipped marginally this year (Tasmac does not officially disclose its Deepavali sales figures. The data has been collated from various sources for several years).

While some salesmen attributed the dip in sales to machines getting stuck and confusion surrounding the buy back scheme, others said that liquor sales had been unusually high over the past week, with crowds slightly larger than usual. “People were worried that shops might not open because of the issues surrounding the buy back scheme. So, many started stocking up for the festival as early as last week,” said a salesman at a shop in the T. Nagar region.

A senior Tasmac official said that the issues with POS machines would be resolved soon and that around 1,000 new POS machines would be deployed across outlets soon. “Wherever there is a requirement we will deploy these machines.” the official added.
When asked about the issues with POS machines, Minister for Prohibition and Excise K. Vignesh questioned: “The POS machines were working until November 1. What happened after that?”

He also said that around 44 salesmen had been suspended between November 1 and 5 for violating MRP norms. “We have received more complaints of similar violations and will initiate action on them as well,” he added.

Tasmac sources said the corporation is estimated to have collected around ₹38 crore through the Environment Protection Cess. From November 1, 2026, a ₹10 Environmental and Social Welfare Cess was levied on liquor sales to facilitate the buy back of empty bottles. The cess was included in the MRP.

As on July 2026, Tasmac has 4,048 retail vending shops and a workforce of 22,877 (6,473 supervisors, 14,379 salespersons, and 2,025 assistant salespersons). For the year 2025-2026, Tasmac earned a revenue of ₹50,845 crore.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Kinnauri weaves on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
At the Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Shimla district. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Jewellery on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.

Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.

On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
Kinnauri apples on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Traders at Lavi Fair accept payments via UPI now. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “ chilgoza , the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 10 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Without peace, Israel risks descending into chaos

Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

articles.title: Postpone panchayat, municipal elections to April-May next year: Ladakh group
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “We suspect that this government is up to some mischief. We saw ‘vote chori’ in West Bengal, Bihar, Haryana, Maharashtra etc. In entire India 13 crore voters were dropped from the voter list. Ladakh is a small region and fraud is easy,” said Ladakh Buddhist Association (LBA) chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook

Several groups in Ladakh on Monday (November 9, 2026) demanded postponement of panchayat and municipal elections and alleged the authorities were up to some mischief in the region, which saw street agitation over the demands of Statehood and Sixth Schedule in the past six years. Meanwhile, a shutdown call has been issued in Kargil over the election.

“We suspect that this government is up to some mischief. We saw ‘vote chori’ in West Bengal, Bihar, Haryana, Maharashtra etc. In entire India 13 crore voters were dropped from the voter list. Ladakh is a small region and fraud is easy,” said Ladakh Buddhist Association (LBA) chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook.

Terming the upcoming panchayat and municipal elections as “conspiracy against people of Ladakh”, Mr. Lakrook, who is also co-chairman of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), said, “I warn people of Ladakh that these elections are a conspiracy. People of Ladakh should stay awake. We demand postponement of these elections. Let the authorities first frame the constituencies and hold the election in April-May next year,” said Mr. Lakrook.

The Lieutenant Governor administration of Ladakh last month dissolved the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC)-Kargil and announced panchayat and municipal elections on November 21 and the process shall be completed before November 30, officials said.
“The back-to-back elections are held in a hurry. These elections will see greater participation if held next year,” said Mr. Lakrook.
Meanwhile, Mr. Lakrook said there will be an agitation in the region and accused the Centre of taking the civil society groups, holding talks with it, “for granted”.

“In a few days, an agitation will be launched. We will show how much support we have. In the past, villages were cut off in the name of official functions and were later portrayed as poor participation in our programmes. This time, the agitation will sustain. We will have to struggle and be ready for sacrifices. I ask all to shun any sense of fear,” said Mr. Lakrook.

The Centre-Ladakh talks hit a wall in October this year after the Centre decided against the proposed meeting with the Ladakh civil society group in Delhi on October 22, days after a draft proposal on roadmap by the Centre was criticised by these groups.

In Kargil, the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), a conglomerate of socio-political groups, called for a “complete shutdown” across Kargil on November 10 in protest against the deferment of hill council elections.

“I urge the Lieutenant Governor and the State Election Commissioner (SEC) to consider Ladakh’s geographical and climatic conditions before scheduling polls. Elections in winter could deprive many people of their right to vote. I have also submitted written objections regarding the delimitation exercise,” said Ladakh Member of Parliament (MP) Haji Haneefa.
The KDA has called for a march to “Save Democracy” in Ladakh and appealed locals to respond positively to the call.

articles.title: Bengaluru family murders: All seven bodies recovered
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The latest breakthrough came on Monday (November 9, 2026), with the police recovering two more bodies from Shiradi Ghat, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.

In a significant development in the case of the murders of seven members of a family, which has sent shockwaves across Karnataka, the police have now successfully recovered all seven bodies. The recovery of the bodies was a crucial step in the probe into the ghastly murders, to build a strong case.

The latest breakthrough came on Monday (November 9, 2026), with the police recovering two more bodies from Shiradi Ghat, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka. The bodies have been identified as those of Shankar, the accused Indushekhar’s brother-in-law and his wife, Nalini, who were among the seven victims.

The development comes a day after the police recovered two bodies of the accused’s brother-in-law, Shivakumar and his wife, Divya, from the foothills of Chamundi Hills on Sunday (November 8, 2026). A day before that, the police had recovered two more bodies of the accused’s wife, Sunita and her mother, Roopavathi, from Salem, Tamil Nadu. On November 6, they had recovered the body of a minor boy, Puneeth, 7, from the foothills of Nandi Hills.

The families have decided to conduct the last rites for all seven together in one place. The bodies, most of them found in a highly decomposed state, will be handed over to the family after autopsies have been conducted.

Following a missing complaint by the deceased Nalini’s mother, Tungamma, the Srirampura police on November 5 detained Indushekhar and his 17-year-old minor daughter and rescued an 11-year-old boy from them. The duo confessed to having killed seven members of their family. Indushekhar’s wife, mother-in-law, two brothers-in-law, and their families. The accused has reportedly claimed that marital discord and humiliation by his wife’s family spurred him to take revenge.

articles.title: Ethanol blend row: Minister stands firm on claim, demands independent fuel testing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: It was the OMC laboratories’ failure to provide the required result that raised suspicion; the samples were then sent to NABL-accredited and ISO-certified laboratories, says Rizwan Arshad
Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Rizwan Arshad on Monday said that he stands by the test reports on ethanol blending in petrol that were released by him on November 6.

Addressing the media on Monday, Mr. Arshad said, “We stand by our test reports as the tests were done as per the prescribed procedure in laboratories recognised by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), which is a constituent board of the Quality Council of India (QCI).”

He added, “As an elected government, I was expecting an official response from the Union government, whereas they have made the oil companies respond to us. I have examined their statements on our E20 findings. The OMCs’ release is more about technicalities, but they have failed to answer how much ethanol is in the petrol at our pumps.”

The Minister had on November 6 released the test reports of 63 petrol samples collected from petrol bunks across Karnataka. Of the 63 samples, those from Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) showed ethanol-blending levels of more than 20%, at 31.2%, 30.5% and 24.2%, respectively.
He slammed the oil companies for stating that the samples were not tested as per the prescribed procedure and that the laboratories used for testing were not those specified under the Order.

“The initial 63 samples were first given to the OMCs’ own laboratories at IOCL, BPCL and HPCL for testing. Not one of their test reports stated the ethanol percentage. IS 17021:2018, the standard the OMCs themselves cite, clearly lays down the procedures for testing ethanol content. Yet not a single OMC report gave that figure. It was the OMC laboratories’ failure to provide the required result that raised suspicion. On no grounds can the State’s tests be discredited for this. To protect consumers, the samples were then sent to NABL-accredited and ISO-certified laboratories,” he said.

Highlighting concerns raised by vehicle manufacturers, he said, “On July 28, 2026, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) wrote to the Union Petroleum Ministry flagging chloride and sulphur in E20 fuel and the damage it was causing to vehicle parts. Within a week, amid pressure from the Centre, the letter was withdrawn. ACKO Insurance told a customer that engine damage from ‘incorrect fuel usage’ would not be covered under insurance. Hyundai, Toyota and other automobile manufacturers wrote in their manuals that using fuel other than E10 would void the warranty.”

The Minister also noted that the report on the same subject by the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) remains hidden from the public. He added that the Attorney General had told the Supreme Court that E20 was still an experiment, but later issued a clarification.
He said the Karnataka government cannot be silenced and will not step back like industry bodies, companies and other individuals who, he claimed, had been silenced or may step back due to pressure.

Mr. Arshad also expressed his disapproval of the Union government’s call for a joint inspection of E20 blending in petrol. He said, “A few months ago, when I wrote to the Union government seeking inspection and testing, they did not respond. Now, when the test reports are out, they are asking for a joint inspection. What is the point of conducting an inspection after setting the system right?”

Responding to the OMCs’ statement that the problem exists only in samples collected from particular petrol pumps and not elsewhere, the Minister said, “The OMCs’ own statement says ethanol blending is ‘a controlled and automated process’ carried out at their refineries and depots. If so, the blend in every litre of petrol is decided at the OMCs’ six terminals serving Karnataka, not at the pump. A dealer only sells what the tanker delivers and has no role in the blend. The excess ethanol found is a failure at the source, and the responsibility lies with the OMCs alone.”
He maintained that by conducting this exercise and exposing these gaps in the OMCs’ systems, the Karnataka government has created a sense of deterrence across the country.

articles.title: Policeman beaten to death in Theni over Deepavali celebration dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Special Police Sub-Inspector Senthilkumar was killed while questioning a gang who were filming reels about bursting firecrackers on the road on November 8 night.
A Special Sub-Inspector of Police (SSI) was beaten to death by a gang of youths when he questioned them for disrupting traffic at Samadharmapuram in Theni Allinagaram on Deepavali day.

According to the police, SSI Senthilkumar, 55, attached to the office of the Theni Deputy Superintendent of Police, was returning home after duty when he noticed the seven-member gang bursting firecrackers in the middle of the road and making reels on Sunday night.
The SSI, who was wearing civilian clothes, scolded the youths and asked them to burst the firecrackers on the roadside.

As the youths, who were in an inebriated state, did not heed his advice, Senthilkumar began recording their activities on his mobile phone. Angered by this, the youths beat him up, rendering him unconscious.
He was rushed to a private hospital in a police patrol vehicle. As his health deteriorated, he was taken to the Theni Government Medical College hospital, where he was declared ‘brought dead’.
The Theni police had arrested six out of the seven accused, a police officer said.
AIADMK, AMMK leaders lash out at CM Vijay over Deepavali day murders across Tamil Nadu
Quarrel over bursting Deepavali crackers ends in youth’s murder in Tiruchi district
18-year-old youth murdered by gang in Chennai’s Vyasarpadi

A statement from the Theni district police said the SSI had attempted to apprehend one of the youths bursting firecrackers on the road. Another youth had elbowed Senthilkumar, causing him to lose balance and fall.
An earlier police statement had said the SSI had a heart-related ailment.

Meanwhile, Senthilkumar’s mortal remains were cremated in Theni after a post-mortem. He was accorded a gun-salute, in the presence of Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) T.S. Anbu, Inspector General of Police (South Zone) Vijayendra Bidari, and Superintendent of Police K.S. Praveen Gowtham.

articles.title: Building over Srinagar’s future
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Suspend the FAR and land-use exemptions, along with Section 22, until they are brought within the Master Plan framework and subjected to public objections

Two conversations about the Himalayas are running at the same time, and they are not converging. Everyone agrees that mountain towns are reaching their limits in different ways, springs are drying up, lakes are choking, and slopes are giving way. No hill town should approve large construction before measuring what it can carry. Yet the developmental model is running parallel. Recent notifications and bills in Jammu and Kashmir are making it easier to build more, on more land. Srinagar is being overwhelmed by that.

Let us start with a simple idea. Floor Area Ratio (FAR) determines how much floor space can be built on a plot. On a 100-square-metre plot, an FAR of 200% allows 200 square metres of floor space. When the number is raised, the same plot must hold more people, cars, toilets, drains, etc. Over nine months, the rules have been repeatedly changed. The building by-laws were amended on December 1, 2025. On July 24, 2026, they were extended to Housing Board colonies, with additional FAR and reduced setbacks. On September 9, fresh limits were proposed, including an FAR of 300% for commercial complexes. On September 28, the Ease of Doing Business Bill, 2026, was tabled. In the first week of October, the Lieutenant Governor gave his assent, and the Bill became law.
National & Polity Report: Building over Srinagar’s future. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.

articles.title: Wayanad conservationist N. Badusha wins environmental award
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Wayanad Prakruthi Samrakshana Samithi (WPSS) president N. Badusha has been selected for the seventh environmental award instituted by the Dr. Kamarudeen Foundation for Biodiversity Conservation (KFBC).

articles.title: Nvidia plunges but tech shares rebound, oil prices slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia shares slumped more than 8% as trading got under way in New York but recovered to stand down more than 5% in early afternoon trading

Technology share prices clawed back last week's sharp losses on Monday (November 9, 2026), despite a plunge in Nvidia following a probe into its boss Jensen Huang over claims of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Oil prices fell over 5% on hopes for diplomatic talks aimed at ending the U.S.-Iran war, before paring losses.

Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after last Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress, leading to speculation lawmakers would seek to rein in tech firms.
But Wall Street on Monday (November 9, 2026) rebounded, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing more than 2%.
Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare said the rebound in equities was due to more than just the drop in oil prices.
"What we also have this morning is an inclination to buy into last week's weakness, and specifically into the large losses seen in the AI trade," he said in a note to clients.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which includes major chipmakers and AI firms, jumped more than 6%.
But the gains did not extend to Nvidia, which saw its shares slump more than 8% as trading got under way in New York, but recovered to stand down more than 5% in early afternoon trading.
Mr. O'Hare said Nvidia was being treated as a one-off story by investors for the moment.

"In other words, the stock is being penalized for Jensen Huang's personal transgression, which has invited a great deal of uncertainty into the mix, but the market isn't caught up in the notion that this situation is going to have a systemic domino effect," he said.

The news that Nvidia's board would investigate whether Mr. Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot, following his admission he was unfaithful to his wife, brought fresh uncertainty in the markets.

The New York Times last month reported that U.S. intelligence officials concluded a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed had been funnelling information to Beijing.

articles.title: Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinised after foreign intelligence concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley

U.S. President Donald Trump’s close relationship with embattled ‌Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday (November 9, 2026), after the company ​said its board was investigating whether the tech executive has been the target ⁠of a foreign intelligence effort.

Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates to at least 2025. Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support ‌for the administration’s agenda and become a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.
Advanced chips are the backbone of ‌the U.S. AI boom and government officials have previously tried to restrict China’s access to ‌them ⁠through export controls to stifle its AI capabilities.

Nvidia’s board launched its probe after ⁠a New York Times report said Mr. Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials believe passed information to the Chinese government. Nvidia shares hit a seven-month low on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. Huang has a direct line to the ​president. A Reuters reporter saw Huang’s full ‌name pop up on Mr. Trump’s phone in December 2025.

Mr. Huang flew with Mr. Trump to China on Air Force One in May, the first visit by a U.S. president to China in nearly a decade. Mr. Huang attended a high-profile state dinner in September for Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping at the White House. The company committed $25 million for Mr. Trump’s planned ​White House ballroom, according to media reports.

The New York Times reported that Mr. Trump was briefed on Mr. Huang’s relationship with the woman and that she was giving information ⁠to the Chinese government, and chose not to act on the information.
Neither the White House nor Nvidia’s communications team immediately responded to a Reuters request for comment on their relationship.

“I’m pushing to investigate ‌Jensen Huang and Nvidia to determine whether our national security was compromised,” said Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, in a post on X. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration, who’s making these decisions, and who’s really got their hand on the wheel.”

Mr. Huang’s relationship with Mr. Trump has coincided with several favourable policy developments for the company. In April 2025, the administration backed off plans to restrict exports of certain Nvidia AI chips to China ‌after Mr. Huang attended a dinner at Mr. Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.
In December 2025, Mr. Trump said the U.S. would ​allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors, its second-best AI chips, to China and collect a 25% fee on such sales.

Mr. Trump has lavished Mr. Huang with praise, ⁠awarding him the nation’s highest honour for scientific achievement in October. The same day Mr. Trump gave Mr. Huang the ⁠award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million in Nvidia stock during the summer.

articles.title: Hegseth faces expected U.S. House impeachment vote this week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday, setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power

Pete Hegseth, the U.S. Defence Secretary, calls himself the Secretary of War, part of his effort to rebrand ‌a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year. Now, with ​a House impeachment vote expected this week, he could soon share something in common with an ⁠actual secretary of war.
William Belknap, who held that title in 1876, became the first, and to date only, civilian leader of the U.S. military to be impeached by Congress.

U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday (November 9, 2026), setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power.

Congressional sources say the resolution may have the simple majority needed to pass the Republican-controlled ‌House before Democrats take over on January 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds ‌majority ⁠is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats.
House Speaker Mike Johnson opposed the effort, saying impeachment “in ⁠the middle of hostilities abroad” would be “a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see.”

Voter anger over the war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections, intensifying Republican divisions over a conflict that Vice-President J.D. Vance has publicly questioned and Mr. Hegseth has ​defended as “courageous and historic.”

Accused of taking huge kickbacks, ‌Belknap handed President Ulysses Grant his resignation ahead of his scheduled impeachment vote and, according to a Senate history, “burst into tears.” The House impeached him anyway, but the Senate later acquitted him after falling short of the required two-thirds majority.
By contrast, Mr. Hegseth is promising to stay and fight.

Mr. Hegseth has mounted a social media campaign, saying ‌in a defiant video message last week that he would not back down. He also drew a ​comparison to President Donald Trump, who was impeached twice, saying: “It didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”

Asked if he had enough Republican support to defeat the impeachment push, Mr. Hegseth ⁠said on Monday (November 9, 2026): “We’re not worried about that.” He announced a Tuesday (November 10, 2026) press conference, his first at the Pentagon since May.
Mr. Trump has backed Mr. Hegseth and condemned the impeachment push in an interview with CBS ’s “60 Minutes” broadcast on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
“They want to impeach him. ‌Very unfair. We had two wars, we won both,” Mr. Trump said, according to a CBS transcript of the full interview.

articles.title: A case for Nepal: suing major carbon emitters for floods
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While climate wrongs harm society, they do not harm individuals in a sufficiently direct and proximate way

The catastrophic floods in Nepal which resulted in the deaths of thousands of people in August 2026, is overwhelmingly attributed to climate change. This is yet another worst-case climate change scenario from South Asia, after the floods in Pakistan in 2022.

A debate that has not drawn much attention so far in this part of the world is that there is scope to explore and establish the flood victims as victims of climate wrongs. The case for the Nepalese people needs to be analysed from the prism of climate litigations used by plaintiffs in many jurisdictions of Europe and the U.S. in the last two decades.

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Missing PM2.5 data for several hours on CPCB website understated city’s pollution levels: experts; 227 PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 stations; govt. will look into it: Mishra

Air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with experts warning that the gaps have led to understated pollution levels and resulted in a lower official air quality index (AQI).

According to Dr. D. Saha, former head of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)’s air quality laboratory, AQI values are calculated using a moving or running average of hourly concentrations of eight parameters, including PM2.5 and PM10, over the previous 24 hours.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), PM2.5 data were missing for several hours at many stations in the city, including Anand Vihar, Patparganj and Bawana, on the CPCB website. PM2.5 (particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter) consists of fine inhalable particles that can penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream, causing respiratory and other diseases. Similar data gaps were reported at several monitoring stations during Deepavali last year as well.

Manoj Kumar, an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finland-based non-profit research organisation, said the missing hourly PM2.5 data “raised concerns about the assessment of Delhi’s air quality”.

“From midnight on November 8 until 5 a.m. on November 9, 227 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation,” Mr. Kumar said, adding, “When the hourly PM2.5 data is missing, it will artificially lower the AQI, showing better air quality when the actual air quality is worse.”

When asked about the missing air quality data at several monitoring stations, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra told the media that the government would look into the issue. The Member Secretary of the CPCB, which releases AQI data, did not respond to calls and messages seeking comment.
Dr. Saha told The Hindu that there should not be gaps in the data, especially during crucial periods.

“If hourly PM2.5 or PM10 value is blank or missing, it will affect the AQI calculated and the final value of the AQI calculated will be less than the actual value of AQI and scientifically incorrect,” Mr. Saha said.

He also said the CPCB had set the measurement range of PM2.5 analysers at 0–1,000 micrograms per cubic metre, which meant they could not measure concentrations above that level. “So, if the value of PM2.5 is beyond 1,000, it should at least be shown as 1,000 instead of showing blank,” he said.

A former DPCC scientist, who did not wish to be identified, said the CPCB recorded PM2.5 values only up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre because there was a minor drop in accuracy at higher levels. “But at very high values, a small drop in accuracy will not matter a lot. Ideally, the CPCB should be measuring the higher values so that we are not missing the peak values,” the official said, adding that not measuring higher concentrations would artificially make air quality appear better.
Bhavreen Kandhari, an environmental activist, alleged that the government was clearly fudging the data to conceal the actual air pollution situation rather than solving the problem.
On the CPCB website, PM2.5 readings appeared to be capped at 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre across all stations, with data missing for several hours at multiple locations.

articles.title: ED attaches properties in Kashmir in ‘misuse’ of PM Employment Generation Programme scheme case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An ED spokesman said there was misappropriation of PMEGP Scheme’s loans in criminal conspiracy with the PMEGP borrowers, bank officials of Sumbal Branch and Gamud Gadkhud Branch of J&K Bank and other unknown persons

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Monday (November 9, 2026) attached the immovable properties worth ₹10.63 crore under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) in alleged misuse of the Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) case.

An ED spokesman said there was misappropriation of PMEGP Scheme’s loans in criminal conspiracy with the PMEGP borrowers, bank officials of Sumbal Branch and Gamud Gadkhud Branch of J&K Bank and other unknown persons.

“The accused have cheated the bank and misappropriated bank funds and caused wrongful loss to the bank and corresponding wrongful gain to themselves. Investigation revealed PMEGP Loans amounts availed by projecting dummy PMEGP borrowers by using fake invoices of non-exist firm/companies and in criminal conspiracy with bank officials branches Sumbal and Gamud Gadkhud of J&K Bank by private persons-cum-brokers,” said the spokesman.
The CBI and J&K’s anti-corruption bureau (ACB) has also registered a case in the matter in June 2026.

The ED said the suspected proceeds derived from the scheduled offences were diverted through bank accounts in multiple transactions and part of it was utilised for construction and renovation of assets and personal enrichment. “Investigation conducted so far, was able to trace the generation of Proceeds of Crime to the tune of Rs. 11.37 crore. Further investigation is under progress,” said the ED.

articles.title: Return of patriarch: Farooq steps in as NC old guard reasserts influence to check Omar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The stand-off between the 17 MLAs of the ruling National Conference (NC) and Kashmir’s first political family, the Abdullahs, has had a rare consequence. It has brought the 89-year-old party patriarch, Farooq Abdullah, back into the saddle to steer the party and shape how the government functions, after he had nearly faded from affairs run entirely by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah.

The stalemate began on October 27 with the CM’s Cabinet reshuffle, after which at least three senior party leaders publicly expressed resentment over not being inducted. Later that day, the disgruntled legislators held a meeting, conspicuously in the absence of the Abdullahs, and subsequently submitted a charter of demands to the party leadership, which included intensifying the struggle for the restoration of Statehood and special status, removing Nasir Aslam Wani as the CM’s Adviser and reassigning the Roads and Buildings portfolio, currently held by Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary.

In seven decades of the NC, the parallel party meeting was seen as a rare implosion and a visible crack that the Opposition parties could exploit to tilt the balance of numbers against the Omar Abdullah government.
The NC has 42 legislators in the 90-member J&K Assembly and the support of eight other MLAs.

The stand-off appears to have ended following a two-hour meeting on November 6 between the dissenting legislators and the party brass ahead of Friday prayers, which saw Mr. Farooq taking the lead role.
“Our struggle for Statehood, Articles 370 and 35A will continue,” he later told mediapersons in Srinagar.
On Monday, NC’s newly inducted Minister Mir Saifullah underlined that sentiment, saying the “struggle had started”.

“Whatever has been snatched will be taken back. It was the NC who got pre-1953 status, Article 370 and separate flag for J&K. The struggle for their return has begun. We all start from zero but will reach 100 one day,” he said at a rally in north Kashmir’s Kupwara.
Ever since Mr. Omar took over as the CM for the first time in 2009, there has been an apparent waning of the influence of the old guard in decision-making in the party as well as the government.

After Mr. Omar, who has served as the NC president twice while his father has headed the party four times, came to power as the CM in 2024, the old guard remained out of Cabinet as well as the government.

His detractors view Mr. Omar’s confidants — Mr. Wani; Shammi Oberoi, the first-ever Sikh to be sent to the Rajya Sabha from the Valley; and Tanvir Sadiq, an MLA and party spokesperson — as his only eyes and ears.
Behind the curtain, senior leaders have often spoken about Mr. Omar becoming inaccessible.

articles.title: U.K. writer M. John Harrison wins Booker for AI-tinged apocalyptic novel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: M. John Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize

U.K. author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday (November 9, 2026) for his enigmatic novel "The End of Everything", which echoes concerns about artificial intelligence in a darkly satirical depiction of post-apocalyptic Britain.
Mr. Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize and a boost in sales and profile for the winner.
Review | ‘The End of Everything’ by M. John Harrison: the aliens are here
A veteran of the British science fiction literary scene, it was Mr. Harrison’s first time being shortlisted for the coveted prize, which critics have said was long overdue.

He beat shortlisted authors Marlon James, Douglas Stuart, Elizabeth Strout, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry, whose entries ranged from a queer epic unfolding in 1980s Kingston to a campus satire set in modern-day London.
"The End of Everything" came out "ahead in terms of both its extraordinary expert writing, but also huge ambition," chair of the judges Mary Beard told a press conference.

Mr. Harrison's 13th novel follows the beachcomber Phillip Tennent and his dementia-stricken, free-spirited aunt Marnie, set in the near-future on the windswept English coast invaded by mysterious objects known as the iGhetti.

An unnamed catastrophe plunges the characters into a murky post-apocalyptic world where the European continent seems to have disappeared and the arrival of the iGhetti, which can imitate humans, evoke interactions with artificial intelligence.
"One main point of the book is that if, or when, such an apocalypse comes it will be incomprehensible," Ms. Beard said, adding the book spoke to the present "moment".
"This is the politics of now seen through the lens of the future," Ms. Beard said in a statement.
In dream-like episodes this tight, 198-page novel alludes to Brexit, the COVID-19 pandemic and the invasion of technology into daily life.

As is often the case with Mr. Harrison's writing, which has been described as genre-bending and singular, the plot counts less than the atmosphere, and the author's elliptical and poetic style heightens the feeling of gradual collapse.

articles.title: Trinamool MLA Paresh Ram Das arrested on charges of rape and extortion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several leaders of the Trinamool Congress have been arrested after the BJP came to power in May 2026, which includes five former Ministers

Mamata All India Trinamool Congress MLA Paresh Ram Das was arrested on Monday (November 9, 2026) from Kolkata’s Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Police said there were several charges against the Canning Paschim MLA including extortion and rape.

According to police sources, the Special Operations Group (SOG) of Baruipur district police began tracking the MLA after receiving information that he was heading to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Mr. Das had defeated his nearest rival, BJP candidate from Canning Paschim by a margin of over 40,000 votes.

The team subsequently contacted the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate, following which the MLA was arrested. Mr. Das is among the handful of MLAs that have remained with former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.

Mamata AITC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said that as he was with the rebel camp, the police were inactive but when the MLA pledged his alliance to Ms. Banerjee, he was arrested. Recently, the MLA has put a post of social media, stating “Alvida Canning. We will meet again”.

Several leaders of the Trinamool Congress have been arrested after the BJP came to power in May 2026, which includes five former Ministers, including Bishnupur MLA Dilip Mondal. The list of former Ministers who are behind bars includes Sujit Bose, Indranil Sen, Ujjwal Biswas and Udayan Guha.

The Mamata Banerjee loyalists claim that leaders, MLAs and former Ministers who have joined the rebel camp led by Ritabrata Banerjee are being given a reprieve by the police while those still having allegiance to the former Chief Minister are being arrested.

articles.title: Outcry as J&K Bank implements reservation policy pushed by ex-chairman and VHP trustee R.K. Chhibber
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The bank has decided to fill 1400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy

The amended reservation policy of the J&K Bank, which was introduced by ex-chairman R.K. Chhibber in 2021-2022, who was later appointed as a Trustee of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), on Monday (November 9, 2026) triggered a political storm with regional political parties, religious and social organisations opposing it, with many terming it “an act of exclusion in the garb of reservation”.

For the first time, the J&K Bank, which provides high-end jobs in a region with a low corporate footprint, is facing a push from the regional parties, including the ruling National Conference (NC). The bank has decided to fill 1400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy. It also reduced the age limit from 32 to 30 for the Open Merit and increased the age criteria for the reserved categories to 40 years.

“The existing upper age limit of 30 years needed reconsideration. The recruitment age limit should be raised to 40 years to provide more opportunities to eligible aspirants,” said J&K Education Minister Shamima Firdous.

The J&K Bank is considered one of the main non-government recruitment agencies of the Union Territory (UT). Around 1.40 lakh locals had applied for 1500 banking associates in 2021-2022 during the tenure of Mr. Chhibber, who later faced allegations of regional imbalance with more candidates selected from the Jammu region against the aspirants from the Kashmir division. In spite of being selected as a trustee of the VHP, Mr. Chhibber continued to be on the Board of Directors till 2026 and remained a key proponent for introducing the new reservation policy.

According to the notification, the bank has decided to open positions to 60% for the reserved categories and 40% for the Open Merit. The reservation policy adopted by the bank recruitment included 8% from the Schedule Caste, 20% from the Schedule Tribe, 8% from the Other Backward Classes, 4% from the Actual Line of Control/International Border, 10 % from the Resident of Backward Area (RBA)and 10% from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).

The J&K Students Association (JKSA) sought intervention of J&K Lieutenant-Governor into the matter. “Only approximately 542 posts fall under Open Merit, while the remaining vacancies are allocated to reserved categories. Merit should remain the cornerstone of recruitment and every eligible candidate must have a fair opportunity to compete. The educated youth of J&K have already endured years of uncertainty and limited employment opportunities. They should not be penalised for circumstances over which they had no control,” reads the letter written by Zubair Reshi, national spokesperson of the JKSA, addressed to the L-G.

The letter demanded that the concerns surrounding the availability of opportunities, equitable representation and the overall recruitment framework “deserve careful examination by the competent authorities”. It pointed out that the bank announcement of fresh recruitment came “after a prolonged gap of nearly six years”.

“The upper age limit has caused widespread disappointment among aspirants. Thousands of young people have invested years of their lives, considerable financial resources and immense effort in preparing for competitive examinations,” it added.

Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) legislator Waheed ur Rehman Parra termed the bank recruitment policy “a concern”. “It’s deeply concerning. The age limit at 20-30 years is completely unfair to thousands of overaged aspirants who have been waiting patiently for years. Applying reservation policies in a commercial institution like J&K Bank undermines meritocracy for our local youth. Revoke reservation in the recruitment. Give our educated youth a fair and equal chance,” said Mr. Parra.

CPI(M) leader has backed the demands of the students. “The government has set the recruitment age at 40 years. Given the rising unemployment in J&K, I request the J&K Bank authorities to reconsider the age criteria and raise the upper age limit, thereby providing an opportunity to more deserving and eligible candidates,” CPI(M) leader M.Y. Tarigami.

J&K grand mufti Nasirul Islam said the recruitment policies must be guided by fairness, inclusivity and a realistic understanding of the challenges faced by our educated youth. “The existing concerns surrounding category-wise age relaxations have added to the anxiety of aspirants, especially those in the Open Merit category, who feel that their aspirations are increasingly constrained,” said Mr. Islam.
He said the recruitment framework must also ensure that the Open Merit candidates “were not left feeling disadvantaged or deprived of a fair opportunity to compete”.

articles.title: Kerala HC allows hotel Radisson Blu in Kochi to operate till 3 a.m.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Murali Purushothaman sets aside notice by police authorities banning the hotel from operating and conducting DJ parties after 11 p.m.
The Kerala High Court has allowed hotel Radisson Blu, Kochi, to operate till 3 a.m.
Justice Murali Purushothaman set aside a notice by police authorities banning the hotel from operating and conducting DJ parties after 11 p.m.

The State had contended that allowing the hotel to operate and conduct DJ parties till 3 a.m. would cause disruptions to public order and act as a venue for drug-related transactions.
