articles.title: Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Myanmar's military has seized a key resistance military command headquarters and 10 other bases in the south of the country, state media reported on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), marking a new gain by the army in the civil war as it seeks control of regions long held by resistance forces.
The capture of the bases in the jungle along the border between Mon state and the Bago region marks the latest setback suffered by pro-democracy armed groups and ethnic militias fighting the army.
The reported capture could not be independently confirmed because the military does not allow journalists free access to the area, but the claim has not been challenged.

The military-backed government, which took office in April following controversial elections earlier this year, has stepped up activity in recent months on the ground and with airstrikes to retake areas controlled by the People's Defense Force, the armed wing of the major opposition National Unity Government, and ethnic militias that have been fighting the central government for greater autonomy for decades.
The PDF emerged after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021 and has since formed loose alliances with ethnic militias fighting the military.

A report in the state-run Myanma Alinn newspaper on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said the army captured 11 bases operating in the jungle area straddling the border between Mon and Bago during a six-day operation that began a week ago.

The captured positions included the special region command headquarters of the NUG and a battalion headquarters of the Karen National Liberation Army, the armed wing of the Karen National Union, a major Karen ethnic rebel group.
The paper published photos showing soldiers who captured the bases alongside ammunition seized during the operation.
Small arms, ammunition supplies, vehicles, drones and computers were captured after four armed engagements, the report said, adding that the military would continue security operations in the region.
The NUG and KNU did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The captured regions, about 120 kilometers (75 miles) northeast of Yangon, the country's largest city, have seen intense conflict since the 2021 military takeover that prompted widespread public protests. The violent suppression of the demonstrations by government security forces triggered an armed resistance that has led to civil war.

The NUG's special region command headquarters said in a previous social media statement that it had 12 PDF battalions, seven drones with specialized support units, as well as six combat and defence units under its command. It also said it was conducting military operations across the southern Kayin and Mon states, as well as the Bago region. Kayin state is also known as Karen state.

articles.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel saying it was responding to stone-throwing.
Moutaz Eyad Daghlas was killed in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, late on Monday (November 9, 2026), the Palestinian health ministry said.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds and took them to hospital, but that Israeli forces blocked access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.
The Israeli military, asked by AFP about the incident, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) it had acted to "thwart stone-hurling and terrorist attacks" in the area.

"The soldiers identified several terrorists who intended to hurl stones at a highway used by Israeli vehicles. This was in an area where stones have recently been hurled at Israeli vehicles," the military said.
"The soldiers responded by firing towards them in order to remove the threat."
Israeli forces have routinely opened live fire on Palestinians including minors who throw stones in the West Bank, which Israel has controlled since 1967.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said Israeli forces killed at least 241 children or teenagers in the territory between the October 7, 2023 attack by Gaza-based Hamas and late June this year.

Violence has increased in recent weeks, especially in the run-up to Israel's October 27 election, before which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had sought to appeal to hardline settlers in the West Bank.
On October 23, Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed by Israeli forces, who later responded with a major operation in the flashpoint city.

Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,116 Palestinians, both civilians and militants, in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, according to an AFP tally based on Palestinian Authority figures.
Palestinian attacks or clashes between Palestinians and Israeli forces have killed at least 51 Israelis during the same period, according to official Israeli figures.

articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

A few kilometres from the entrance to Arunachal Pradesh’s Parong village, an unpaved road winds all the way down to the Siang river. At dusk, all that is visible at the beginning of the dirt road is the glint of freshly painted yellow barricades of the State police and the shine from the silver of the concertina wires that connect the barricades. The Central security forces who guard the check post here have two purposes — to respond to “unrest” and to stop anyone without “clearance” from proceeding to Siang’s waters.

Parong, in Siang district, is one of the three proposed sites identified by the State government for a Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) to begin work on the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).

fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
• Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Air pollution over 50 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 50 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, official data showed.

The level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Akshardham was 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data. This is about 50.73 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic meter for a 24-hour period.
Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives
PM2.5 (Particulate Matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.
The level of PM2.5 in Anand Vihar was 767 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per DPCC data — This is about 51.13 times the WHO permissible limit.
The level of PM2.5 in Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was 702 micrograms per cubic meter, as per DPCC data, which is about 46.8 times the WHO permissible limit.
The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe

Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen's Hodeidah and Sana'a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country, the Indian Embassy in Yemen said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

The broader concern is whether chip demand can translate into supplier revenues if data-centre projects are held up by financing constraints, electricity shortages or regulatory hurdles. Capital Market Laboratories analyst Ophir Gottlieb has argued that slower construction could favour cloud companies with existing infrastructure, even as equipment suppliers face order delays.

Yet underlying demand remains robust. AMD’s data-centre revenue surged 97% year-on-year to $8.55 billion in the September quarter. According to a November 5 Huatai Research analysis, the company expects segment revenue to grow about 50% sequentially in the December quarter. AMD also expects overall revenue growth of more than 80% in 2027, with data-centre operations contributing over 80% of total revenue.

articles.title: Delhi AQI row: AAP alleges data fraud, BJP fires back over Punjab stubble ‘conspiracy’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: When asked about air quality data in Delhi missing in several monitoring stations, Kapil Mishra said that the government will look into the issue within an hour and inform the media about it

BJP leader and Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra on Monday (November 9, 2026) alleged that there was a “conspiracy” in AAP-governed Punjab to set stubble on fire in Punjab on Sunday (November 8, 2026) evening, as per official data.

He alleged that 1,200 stubble burning incidents happened in Punjab on Sunday (November 8, 2026) evening, which was 10 times that of previous days. “We got calls from farmers in Punjab that stubble is being set on fire. Someone is coming and setting stubble on fire and running away, when farmers are celebrating Diwali with their families. This is a very serious issue and a conspiracy against Delhi, Punjab, and farmers,” he said.

Earlier in the day, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Delhi over alleged air quality data “manipulation” by shutting down of air quality monitoring stations.

“The government which shuts down air quality monitoring stations on the night of Diwali, the government that does data fraud, how will you trust such a government?” asked AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj in a video posted on X.

“The government is doing the fraud openly. We had written to the CAQM and CPCB (about the data manipulation). But everyone is silent. This is because everyone is part of this fraud,” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

Last week, the AAP had accused the BJP government of “manipulating” AQI data by spraying water on monitoring stations, and alleged that“fudging” AQI data was not just corruption but life-threatening. The party also wrote to CAQM and CPCB last week, alleging that the Delhi government was manipulating air quality data in the national capital.
When asked about air quality data in Delhi missing in several monitoring stations, Mr. Mishra said that the government will look into the issue within an hour and inform the media about it.

At the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.
Reading from 11:00 a.m. on November 9, 2026, from website of Department of Environment, Government of NCT of Delhi, showing several stations not reporting AQI data.

On Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh plans major overhaul of postgraduate education across 28 universities | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Proposed reforms seek to move beyond conventional, examination-orientated degrees towards interdisciplinary learning, industry exposure, research and emerging technologies

Andhra Pradesh is planning a comprehensive restructuring of postgraduate (PG) education across its 28 State universities, with an emphasis on employability, research, entrepreneurship and regional development. The proposed reforms seek to transform universities from institutions offering largely conventional, discipline-based postgraduate courses into specialised regional knowledge hubs aligned with the State’s economic priorities and emerging global opportunities.

The restructuring proposal, prepared by the Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE), envisages a common academic framework for postgraduate programmes while allowing individual universities to develop distinctive areas of specialisation based on their geographical location, institutional strengths, available faculty and regional requirements.

articles.title: Prashant Kishore’s Brahminical criticism of BJP’s Hindutva
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Jan Suraaj party founder urges Brahmins in Bihar’s Mithila to rethink BJP Hindutva, linking secularism, social justice, and Muslim-OBC political coalitions

Secularism is a modern, constitutional principle. In real-world politics, the manifestation of this principle is tested against a rather narrow yardstick: the fair representation of religious minorities, particularly Muslims. Generally speaking, the English-speaking secularists are unaware of the caste dynamics that come into play in the field operation of representative politics, and they are also resistant to the idea of discussing caste as a determinant.

The intersection of caste representation and religious representation mirrors the intersection of social justice and secularism in electoral politics. The caste dynamics of politics are often manifested as critiques by non-Brahmins against Brahminism. A Brahmin perspective on these dynamics is rare, and that is the reason why Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor’s address to fellow Brahmins in Bihar ’s Mithila region is an extremely valuable opportunity to peer into the emerging thinking within the community. He said BJP’s Hindu communalism, which excludes Muslims from electoral calculations, has cost the Brahmins heavily and asked them to rethink their position.

articles.title: Bengaluru family murders: Two more bodies recovered near Chamundi hills in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues

In a fresh development in the brutal murder of seven members of a family, Rajajinagar Police have recovered two more bodies, suspected to be those of Shivakumar and his wife Divya — the accused Indushekhar’s brother-in-law and sister-in-law — near the foothills of Chamundi Hills in Mysuru, on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Police conducted a spot mahazar of the spot with the accused while recovering the bodies.
With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues.

DCP, North Division said that two more dead bodies found near Chamundi hill forest area are said to be of Shivakumar and Divya. Another special police team has been deployed to Shiradi Ghat, where it is conducting searches for the two more missing bodies, he said.

On Saturday (November 7, 2026), police recovered the bodies of the accused’s wife, Sunita, and mother-in-law, Rupavathi, from a forest area in Salem, Tamil Nadu. The body of a young boy was earlier recovered near the foothills of Nandi Hills and has already been cremated.

According to the investigation, Indushekhar allegedly murdered seven of his relatives, including his wife, over a period of 15 days. He is suspected to have packed the bodies in gunny bags, transported them in his car and dumped them at different locations, including the foothills of Nandi Hills, a forest area in Salem, the foothills of Chamundi Hills and Shiradi Ghat.

The accused, who is currently in police custody, is being subjected to intensive interrogation as investigators try to establish the sequence of murders, the motive and the locations where the remaining bodies were disposed of.

articles.title: Jean Drèze urges T.N. govt. to take strict action amid report of ‘fake book’ at Kalaignar Centenary Library
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” the economist said in a clarification via e-mail to The Hindu
Economist Jean Drèze on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said an English-language book attributed to him as the author and allegedly found in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu is “fake”.

The confirmation comes following a media report alleging that a title listed in Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library may not have been authored by Mr. Drèze. The book which lists him as the author, was identified as the title ‘ Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World’’.

“I am foxed and baffled to read on social media that a book called Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World, attributed to me, has surfaced in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu. If this book exists under my name, it must be fake, because I have never authored such a book,” he wrote in a clarification issued to The Hindu via e-mail.

Mr. Drèze urged the Tamil Nadu government to take “strict and swift action against the publishers of this fake book and other culprits”. “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” he added.

The economist also raised questions on procurement checks in place at public libraries and said: “The issue is not just that a fake book was printed but also how it was procured by a public library. Surely it would have taken little effort to ascertain the authenticity of this book.”

According to the media report, the book in question was allegedly procured from Phoenix Publishers and carries a valid International Standard Book Number. It also further alleged that the address of Phoenix Publishers is the same as that of Akal Vilakku Publishers.

The procurement date cited in the report is June 25, 2023 before the inauguration of the library. Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library was inaugurated on July 15, 2023, by the then Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin.

articles.title: Why can’t helicopters be used for sea drowning rescue operations, asks Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan suo motu implead Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in a habeas corpus plea related to a 17-year-old reportedly swept away by high tides

The Madras High Court has questioned why helicopters cannot be pressed into service for drowning rescue operations at the Marina and other beaches spread along the East Coast in Chennai and Chengalpattu districts as well as the coastal zones in other districts.

Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and Justice B. Karthikeyan raised the query during the hearing of a habeas corpus petition filed by K. Gopal of Madhavaram in Chennai. The petitioner’s 17-year-old son G. Santhosh had gone for swimming in the Marina on July 5, 2026 but had not returned since then.

Impressing upon the need for the Central as well as State agencies to work in coordination in the operations to rescue those who get swept away by high tides, the judges suo motu impleaded the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) headed by the Director General of Indian Coast Guard.

They requested Additional Solicitor General AR.L. Sundaresan to obtain instructions from the newly-impleaded respondent by November 20 with respect to the nature of action taken by the central body to rescue those who venture into the sea and get swept away.

Answering a volley of other questions thrown by the judges, Additional Public Prosecutor (APP) M. Mohamed Riyaz told the court that as many as 50 police personnel from the 12 th battalion of Tamil Nadu Special Police get deployed every day at the Marina Beach to control the crowd.

Seven jet skis, an all terrain motor vehicle and two mini tractors were also maintained in Chennai Division for the safety of people who visit the beaches. Further, two 12 ton boats belonging to Coastal Security Group keep patrolling the coast from Pazhaverkadu to Neelankarai, the APP said.

When Justice Chandira wanted to know about the operation of CCTV cameras in the city limits, he was told that the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) was spread over 426 sq.km and that the civic body had installed 468 surveillance cameras in public places across the city limits.

On learning that 73 of those cameras were dysfunctional, the Division Bench wrote: “Cameras not being in a functional state, whatever be the reason, cannot be countenanced. Needless to state that the core raison d’être for installation of CCTV cameras is to ensure alacritous action following an untoward incident. When the CCTV cameras remain non-functional, then, the very object behind installation becomes otiose, for which, the Chennai Corporation becomes answerable.”

The judges said, the issue gains importance since the petitioner’s son remains missing till date though two of his friends, who had gone along with him for swimming in the Marina beach, had been rescued. They insisted upon putting in place an effective mechanism in which the central as well as the State agencies could spring into action in no time to save the lives of fishermen and others who get caught in the high tides.
The Bench decided to hear the MRCC functioning under the National Maritime Search and Rescue Coordinating Authority on November 20 before passing further orders in the case.

articles.title: Oil falls as Donald Trump says new Iran attacks ‘unlikely’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: On November 8, 2026, ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman

Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President ​Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ‌attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both ​nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ⁠the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels ‌per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an ⁠interview with Al Jazeera.
He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 ‌billion.
Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: Who is Alice Huang, Chinese executive accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International
Tech executive Alice Huang is the woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang , head of U.S. artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, according to media reports.
Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International.

Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia boss, according to the New York Times, which first reported that Jensen Huang was the alleged target of a spy plot.
Despite their shared surname, Alice Huang is no relation to the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born head of the world’s most valuable company.
The Times, citing people briefed on the surveillance, said that Alice Huang speaks good English and is well connected at the highest level of the global AI chip industry.
The sector is highly sensitive as the United States and China race to develop advanced AI systems with potential military applications.

An online search brought up a short profile for Alice Huang, with her photo, on a Chinese fund database. It listed previous jobs including at HSBC bank, and as a reporter for Chinese media outlets CCTV and Hunan TV.
AFP was unable to verify the contents of the profile, or who had written it, but has attempted to contact the companies cited.
Media reports last week said they had a close relationship, and Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on Sunday he was “deeply sorry” for being “unfaithful to my wife”.
One photo from an industry party in 2024, posted on LinkedIn, appears to show the leather jacket-clad Nvidia boss sitting next to a long-haired woman in glitzy jewellery believed to be Alice Huang.
The following year, they both attended a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo.
Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees.

articles.title: Bangladesh Foreign Ministry examining Sheikh Hasina’s request for new passport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Deposed PM Sheikh Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she fled to India in August 2024 following the uprising that toppled her government

The Bangladesh High Commission has received a request from deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina for a fresh passport, a source in Dhaka told The Hindu. The official said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs was examining the letter and would take a decision after internal consultations. Ms. Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she fled to India in August 2024 following the uprising that toppled her government.

“We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London, seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the contents of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation,” the source told The Hindu over the phone.

Ms. Hasina held a press conference at the Foreign Correspondents’ Club on August 5 this year, where she announced her intention to return to Bangladesh in December. This was followed by repeated assertions by Awami League leaders based in India that she would act on her announcement. According to Awami League sources, Ms. Hasina may choose to return through one of the land ports along the India-Bangladesh border, including Benapole-Petrapole.

Ms. Hasina has been living in New Delhi since she was ousted in a student-led uprising in July-August 2024. The movement began as a protest against the abolition of the quota system, which reserved government jobs for descendants of those who fought in the 1971 Liberation War. It escalated into a broader protest against Ms. Hasina after a police crackdown in mid-July 2024 left hundreds of students and other civilians dead. The unrest ultimately led to her flight from Bangladesh on August 5.

In November 2025, the International Crimes Tribunal, a special tribunal, sentenced Ms. Hasina to death. The verdict was subsequently criticised because it was delivered in her absence, without representation from Ms. Hasina or her legal team.
Ms. Hasina has so far refused to apologise for the police crackdown. In a written interview with The Hindu earlier this year, she defended the police response, saying

“When police are working in the field, how can they contact the Prime Minister for every action? Police operate under standard operating procedures. They are trained to handle emergencies, crowd control and violent situations. When police personnel were attacked and killed, and police stations were set on fire, they responded according to the situation. How could I personally order officers in those circumstances? The police handle such situations under their SOP.”

articles.title: Revised MRPs of 1,364 anti-cancer formulations come into effect; consumers to save ₹3,540 crore/year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: According to the Ministry, 85 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRPs for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations across 121 drugs as of November 8, 2026

Revised Maximum Retail Prices (MRPs) of 1,364 anti-cancer formulations have come into effect from Monday (November 9, 2026), a move projected to save consumers an estimated ₹3,540.38 crore annually, according to an official release.

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), functioning under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, capped trade margins on the MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs based on recommendations submitted on October 17, 2026, by an Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
According to the Ministry, 85 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRPs for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations across 121 drugs as of November 8, 2026.

Price reductions of over 50% have been reported for 679 brands, with the highest price cut recorded at 96.45%, the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers: Department of Pharmaceuticals said in the release.
The Ministry stated that no chemist or hospital pharmacy is permitted to charge more than the revised MRP.
Consumers can verify medicine rates via the revised MRP printed on packs, the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' mobile application, or the official NPPA website (nppa.gov.in), it said.

Consumers can lodge complaints against instances of overcharging or other pricing-related issues through the Pharma Jan Samadhan portal or contact the NPPA helpline at 1800-111-255, the release added.

articles.title: Google says new Australian internet safety bill could cut off under-18s from Gmail
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Online companies ⁠and free speech advocates say the law could give regulators too much discretion to decide what is harmful, placing ​pressure on platforms to ‌take down content

A proposed Australian internet law could force Google to block under-18s from ​using its Gmail service, an Australia-based company policy ‌head said on Monday, underscoring an industry warning ​that the draft regulation risks overreach.

Under ⁠the Digital Duty of Care legislation, which has already passed Australia’s House of Representatives but needs cross-party support to ‌pass the Senate, internet companies must show they are taking steps to weed ‌out harmful content or face a fine ‌of ⁠up to A$109 million ($75.1 million).

Online companies ⁠and free speech advocates say the law could give regulators too much discretion to decide what is harmful, placing ​pressure on platforms to ‌take down content. Google’s warning reflects concern that the law could filter into everyday parts of the internet.

A section of the law ‌requiring age checks if there was a risk ​of a child seeing pornography “could require us to age assure and block ⁠access to everyday communication services like messaging, email and private file storage”, said Rachel Lord, head of ‌policy in Australia and New Zealand for Google’s YouTube streaming website, at a Senate hearing.
“We are talking about potentially intrusive monitoring within private communications or file storage,” she added.

Representatives from Meta, TikTok and Snap voiced similar concerns, warning ‌the bill could chill online communications by allowing regulators ​broad discretion to determine what content or conduct is harmful while replacing some ⁠existing mandatory industry codes.
Several argued the uncertainty created a ⁠risk platforms would over-moderate content to avoid large regulatory penalties.
The government has said a ‌broad set of rules is the only way to ensure a safe internet.

articles.title: Willem Einthoven’s Nobel-winning discovery that laid the foundations of the modern ECG
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Willem Einthoven’s development of the string galvanometer transformed the recording of cardiac electrical signals and laid the foundations of modern electrocardiography
In 1924, Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for his discovery of the mechanism of the electrocardiogram (ECG)”.

His work made it possible to record the electrical activity of the heart with greater accuracy. By developing the string galvanometer and establishing a standard method for interpreting its recordings, Einthoven helped turn electrocardiography into an important tool for studying heart function. Today, the ECG is routinely used to investigate irregular heart rhythms, detect signs of reduced blood supply to the heart muscle and identify evidence of previous heart attacks.

articles.title: Air pollution over 66 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Data on air pollution missing from several monitoring stations of the Delhi Government at the peak of air pollution during the intervening night of November 8 and 9

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

However, at the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.

Data was unavailable for several hours at multiple stations, including Anand Vihar, R.K. Puram, and Bawana, according to the DPCC website. Data from some other stations had also not been updated since Sunday (November 8) night.
Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives

According to DPCC data, the PM2.5 concentration in Punjabi Bagh stood at 993 micrograms per cubic metre at 4 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 66.2 times the WHO’s recommended 24-hour guideline of 15 micrograms per cubic metre.

In Vivek Vihar, the PM2.5 concentration was 873 micrograms per cubic metre at 2 a.m. on Monday (November 9), about 58.2 times the WHO guideline. In R.K. Puram, it stood at 924 micrograms per cubic metre at 10 p.m. on Sunday (November 8), about 61.6 times the guideline.

PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter. These particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, potentially causing respiratory and other health problems.

Although the Supreme Court had permitted only green firecrackers during specified time windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in Delhi markets.

Delhi’s overall air quality remained in the ‘very poor’ category on Monday (November 9) morning, while several parts of the city continued to record ‘severe’ pollution levels, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
‘Severe’ air pollution affects healthy people and can seriously impact those with existing diseases, the CPCB says.

Delhi’s 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 370, in the ‘very poor’ category, at 9 a.m. on Monday. However, several areas, including Chandni Chowk, ITO, Delhi University’s North Campus, Rohini and Mundka, recorded ‘severe’ air quality.

Every winter, air pollution levels rise across Delhi-NCR and parts of the wider Indo-Gangetic Plain, largely due to meteorological conditions such as low wind speeds and falling temperatures. Emissions from stubble burning in October and November, along with firecracker use during the festive season, add to pollution from vehicles and dust, further deteriorating air quality.

Air pollution over 66 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Data on air pollution missing from several monitoring stations of the Delhi Government at the peak of air pollution during the intervening night of November 8 and 9

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

However, at the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.

Data was unavailable for several hours at multiple stations, including Anand Vihar, R.K. Puram, and Bawana, according to the DPCC website. Data from some other stations had also not been updated since Sunday (November 8) night.

Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives

According to DPCC data, the PM2.5 concentration in Punjabi Bagh stood at 993 micrograms per cubic metre at 4 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 66.2 times the WHO’s recommended 24-hour guideline of 15 micrograms per cubic metre.

In Vivek Vihar, the PM2.5 concentration was 873 micrograms per cubic metre at 2 a.m. on Monday (November 9), about 58.2 times the WHO guideline. In R.K. Puram, it stood at 924 micrograms per cubic metre at 10 p.m. on Sunday (November 8), about 61.6 times the guideline.

PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter. These particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, potentially causing respiratory and other health problems.

Although the Supreme Court had permitted only green firecrackers during specified time windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in Delhi markets.

Delhi’s overall air quality remained in the ‘very poor’ category on Monday (November 9) morning, while several parts of the city continued to record ‘severe’ pollution levels, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.

‘Severe’ air pollution affects healthy people and can seriously impact those with existing diseases, the CPCB says.

Delhi’s 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 370, in the ‘very poor’ category, at 9 a.m. on Monday. However, several areas, including Chandni Chowk, ITO, Delhi University’s North Campus, Rohini and Mundka, recorded ‘severe’ air quality.

articles.title: Karnataka tests petrol samples at 67 locations over ethanol blending complaints: CM Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the CM, inspections had been carried out not only at petrol pumps but also at the stages of ethanol blending and distribution

Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said petrol samples had been collected and tested at 67 locations across the state following complaints that increased ethanol blending was affecting vehicle engine performance.

Speaking to reporters in Bengaluru, Mr. Shivakumar said, “The government has taken serious note of complaints regarding 31.5 per cent ethanol being blended into petrol. Necessary instructions have been issued to the concerned minister in this regard, and information has also been sent to the Central Government.”
Thousands of motorists have complained about various issues, including reduced vehicle mileage, failure to cover expected distances, and engines stalling while in motion, he said.
According to the CM, inspections had been carried out not only at petrol pumps but also at the stages of ethanol blending and distribution.
Documents relating to where and how the blending was being undertaken had also been collected.
“The concerned minister will officially hold a press conference on Monday to provide details regarding the inspection report and the next course of action,” Mr. Shivakumar said.
Holding the Centre responsible for addressing the issue, he said, “The Centre cannot shirk responsibility on this matter. Vehicle performance, fuel quality, and public safety are paramount.”
“It is not right to increase the blending ratio simply to profit from ethanol being available at a lower cost. Causing inconvenience to the public is not acceptable,” he said.
Mr. Shivakumar said his government was taking the complaints seriously and questioned the silence of BJP and JD(S) leaders on the issue.
“Why are BJP and JD(S) leaders, as well as Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka, silent on this issue? Everyone must raise their voice on matters concerning the public interest,” he said.

articles.title: Lab tests show ethanol blend in E20 petrol as high as 31% in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs of Karnataka demands penalising OMCs, an E20 spoilage fund to compensate consumers

Petrol sold by several major oil companies in Karnataka contained ethanol far above the prescribed 20% level, in some cases as high as 31.2%, the Karnataka government has alleged, raising questions about transparency in the ethanol-blended petrol being sold to consumers across the country.

The samples in question were taken recently by the Department of Legal Metrology, under the Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, from Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Tumakuru and Dakshina Kannada districts, said Rizwan Arshad, Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, on Friday.

Petrol samples from major Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), recorded ethanol blend percentages of 31.2% and 30.5%, respectively. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Nayara and Shell petrol samples revealed ethanol blends of 26.5%, 26.1% and 25.5%, respectively, he said.

Mr. Arshad said the samples were initially submitted to the in-house laboratories of IOCL and BPCL. But, he claimed, the test reports issued by these laboratories did not disclose the ethanol content in the fuel, despite it being one of the prescribed testing parameters. “This raises serious concerns about transparency on the part of the oil majors and what they are hiding from consumers,” he said.
Source: Department of Food and Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka

“The Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, later got the same samples tested at laboratories recognised by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) and the International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO). These reports have revealed higher ethanol blends,” Mr. Arshad said.

Mr. Arshad provided copies of six lab test reports from Shriram Research Institute, Bengaluru, a unit of Shriram Tilak Dhar Research Foundation. All six reports showed ethanol blends beyond the permissible 20%.

The Modi Government has already forced E20 petrol on the people, despite serious concerns over reduced mileage, additional fuel expenses and compatibility with older vehicles. Now, what we have uncovered in Karnataka is even more alarming. Our Government's independent laboratory tests have found ethanol content as high as 31.2% in petrol sold by major oil companies, with samples from seven districts exceeding the prescribed 20% limit. Even the Centre has acknowledged that E20 can reduce fuel efficiency in certain vehicles. What happens when the ethanol content goes beyond 30%? Who will bear the additional fuel costs and the risk to vehicle performance? Why should ordinary motorists pay the price for such failures? And look at the Modi Government's double standards: It claims ethanol blending benefits farmers, yet it has now excluded ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from its latest procurement tender. At a time when Karnataka's farmers are already suffering from severe drought, the Centre is restricting an important market for sugarcane-based ethanol while allowing petrol to be sold with ethanol levels far beyond the prescribed limit. Where is the promised benefit to farmers? Where is the protection for motorists? Is this not deceiving both farmers and consumers? Prime Minister @narendramodi and Union Minister @nitin_gadkari owe the people an explanation. When the Union Government itself has prescribed a 20% blending standard, how is petrol containing over 30% ethanol reaching consumers? Who is monitoring these oil companies? Where is the accountability? We will place Karnataka's findings before the Union Government. I demand an immediate investigation, strict action against those responsible, transparent disclosure of ethanol content at every petrol pump and necessary safeguards for consumers.
ALSO WATCH SC refuses plea seeking mandatory E20 ethanol disclosure

Mr. Arshad said 99% of India’s over 35 crore vehicles are not built for ethanol blends of more than 20%, and the risk is not limited to old vehicles. “Vehicles sold after April 2023 have been certified only up to E20. With lower-ethanol-blend petrol withdrawn from nearly one lakh fuel stations, consumers have been left with no alternative,” he said.
Assuming a 10% mileage loss at ₹100 a litre, he said the hidden loss to consumers would amount to around ₹62,000 crore, based on India’s annual fuel consumption of 6,200 crore litres.
The Minister claimed that, after factoring in damage and repair costs due to higher blends, the loss would be around ₹1 lakh crore, but did not elaborate on how he arrived at this figure.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Minister claimed that, after factoring in damage and repair costs due to higher blends, the loss would be around ₹1 lakh crore, but did not elaborate on how he arrived at this figure.

articles.title: No complete closure of Ballari Road for 18 months for elevated corridor work: BDA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period.

The Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road corridor will not be completely closed for 18 months to facilitate the construction of the elevated corridor, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) clarified on Saturday (November 7). Meanwhile, the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) said vehicular movement would continue with limited lane restrictions and phased traffic diversions.

The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period. The elevated corridor is part of the BDA’s larger Integrated Tunnel and Elevated Corridor Project, aimed at easing congestion along the city’s crucial northern corridor connecting Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport. However, the project has also drawn considerable public criticism since it was announced.

The BTP sources said restrictions would apply only to the movement of heavy vehicles between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m., while other motorists would merely be “advised” to take alternative routes. Public transport vehicles and school buses would also be allowed to use the stretch.

The BDA said barricading would be restricted to a lane approximately 4.5 metres wide, affecting only one of the three existing lanes in each direction. The remaining two lanes and the service road would remain open to traffic.

The concern, however, is that the 4.5-metre-wide lane is part of one of the main carriageways and accounts for 35% of the traffic movement on the stretch at any given time. Consequently, the restrictions are likely to worsen congestion, irrespective of the timing of their implementation. At least 20% of the traffic will therefore need to be diverted to prevent gridlock along the stretch.
“Even without civic works, the stretch witnesses prolonged congestion during peak hours. So, with civic works, the need for traffic diversion is essential,” a police source said.

This makes the advisory to use alternative routes necessary. However, the identified alternate routes are also in poor condition. The BTP has now written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and the BDA, requesting them to asphalt the alternative routes to ensure the smooth movement of vehicles and prevent congestion.

“Routes through New BEL Road and R.T. Nagar Station Road are among those being considered for improvement. Officials have also been asked to identify bottlenecks, improve road surfaces, and install adequate signage and road markings,” the BDA said.

articles.title: Keralam power purchase row: BJP leader V. Muraleedharan says CM must clarify if tenders were called
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: MLA says government should also clarify whether private companies other than GNA Energy had approached it and the rates offered by them

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national executive member and MLA V. Muraleedharan has asked Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to clarify whether tenders were invited before the government opted to purchase power from GNA Energy, a digital over-the-counter (OTC) trading platform.

Stressing the need for transparency in the use of government funds at a press conference on Monday, Mr. Muraleedharan said the government should also clarify whether private companies other than GNA Energy had approached it and the rates offered by them.

The “power crisis” in the State, he said, was felt most acutely during peak hours, from 6 p.m. to midnight or 2 a.m. However, the agreement with GNA Energy was for the purchase of power round the clock, and not just during peak hours. According to experts, this would create an additional burden of ₹1,500 crore on the people, he said.

Mr. Muraleedharan asked whether the government would be willing to disclose a comparison of the peak-hour power supply offered by GNA Energy and the Himachal Pradesh government, along with the rates, “in a manner that can be understood by the layman.”

articles.title: Hyderabad: Retired banker’s sketch puts Ladki-Ka-Pul’s one-way traffic plan in motion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hyderabad police say the one-way loops may offer hassle-free experience for commuters with reduced honking; explore this traffic arrangement across the city

A 73-year-old retired bank employee’s hand-drawn map has given Hyderabad Traffic Police an idea they are now seriously examining — a one-way traffic loop around Lakdi-ka-pul and Saifabad. What began as an email suggestion nearly a year ago has progressed to a traffic simulation study and inspections by senior police officers, even as the department explores similar arrangements at other congestion-prone locations across Hyderabad.

Palakodeti Chandrasekhar emailed the police with his proposal to reorganise traffic movement in the busy Lakdi-ka-pul stretch. He was subsequently invited to the Police Commissioner’s office, where he explained the idea. Mr. Chandrasekhar also submitted a hand-drawn map, marking the proposed directions of traffic with arrows.
“I am neither a police officer nor an engineer, and I am certainly no expert at drawing. I sketched the map to the best of my ability,” Mr. Chandrasekhar said.

The sketch maps a proposed loop connecting Lakdi-ka-pul, the Secretariat road, Ravindra Bharathi and the Old Saifabad Police Station, with landmarks such as Dwaraka Hotel, the LIC Building, the Assembly, Public Gardens and the DGP’s office marked along the route.
A view of traffic on Lakdi-ka-pul stretch in Hyderabad. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) D. Joel Davis said the police had conducted a simulation study to assess its feasibility. However, several road improvements would be necessary before even a trial could be introduced. “Certain intersections would have to be developed or modified to ensure smoother movement under the proposed arrangement,” said the officer.

Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar, accompanied by Mr. Davis; DCP Traffic-I Avinash Kumar; ACP Traffic Khairatabad Zone S. Mohan Kumar and Traffic Adviser Venkat Ramaiah, inspected stretches near Dwaraka Hotel, the Old Saifabad Police Station, HDFC, Iqbal Minar and Ravindra Bharathi to assess road conditions and existing traffic patterns.

Mr. Sajjanar said that one-way loops might require motorists to travel a few hundred metres extra, but could make journeys hassle-free, reduce honking and help curb pollution caused by congestion and vehicles remaining stationary with their engines running.

Referring to the one-way arrangement around KBR Park , he said the police had received considerable positive feedback from commuters, particularly about smoother movement and reduced honking. He said there was hardly any honking around KBR Park following the changes. “There were some hiccups initially, but I thank the people of Hyderabad for supporting the initiative. We look forward to better collaboration between the public and the police,” he said.
Hyderabad Police received positive feedback from people about one-way vehicular flow around Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park in Hyderabad. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

In Cyberabad, officials are examining a separate loop connecting Biodiversity Junction, IKEA , Mindspace Rotary, Times Square Road, Knowledge City, Qualcomm, Dallas Centre Road and My Home Bhooja, before reconnecting with Biodiversity Junction.

Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh and Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh inspected the proposed corridor on November 6. Officials were asked to prepare a detailed traffic study covering bottlenecks, traffic generated by buildings and the availability and capacity of parking facilities.
