articles.title: Karnataka milk price hike justified by rising cost of production: D.K. Suresh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: After the latest round of price revision, the farmers are receiving ₹42 as the procurement price per litre, while they also get ₹5 per litre as an incentive

Defending the recent hike in the price of milk and curd by the Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF), the president of Bengaluru Milk Union Ltd., D.K. Suresh, said that if the hike had not been implemented, there were fears of dairy farmers giving up owing to meagre earnings.

Despite the hike in the price of milk in the range of ₹8 to ₹12 per litre and curd by ₹14 a kg, the price of milk was still lower in Karnataka compared to the prevailing price in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana (₹66 a litre), Gujarat (₹57 a litre) and Uttar Pradesh (₹59 a litre), Mr. Suresh told The Hindu on Friday.

“Farmers had been demanding an upward revision of the procurement price for the last six months. The cost of oil cake has increased by up to 80%, while the cost of bran, maize and cattle feed has increased by 49%. The price of maize per tonne has increased from ₹22,000 to ₹35,000 a tonne. The cost of soya cake has increased from ₹35,000 to ₹64,000 a tonne. There is a severe shortage of green fodder. Farmers would have moved away from dairy farming if the procurement price had not been increased,” he said, defending the hike. The Bangalore Urban, Rural and Ramanagara District Co-operative Milk Producers’ Societies Union Ltd. (Bamul) president also said that farmers could start selling milk to private milk dairies that pay them ₹42 per litre.
After the latest round of price revision, the farmers are receiving ₹42 per litre as the procurement price, while they also get ₹5 per litre as an incentive.

Mr. Suresh claimed that the KMF had witnessed an increase in the procurement of milk by about 10 lakh litres after the increase in the procurement price. On average, the KMF is now procuring 1.16 crore litres a day. “Unemployment and migration have also declined as young people are buying one or two cows and selling milk to the KMF. The government incentive of ₹5 per litre is also encouraging dairy farmers. The government spends about ₹2,500 crores annually.”

Elaborating on the cost of producing milk for the district unions, he said that the cost of plastic crates, culture used in curd, fat used in milk, furnace oil, commercial diesel and gas, refrigeration and electricity had all gone up since the war began in West Asia, besides the cost of ESI and Provident Fund. “The cost of furnace oil has gone up by 40%; commercial diesel costs ₹115 a litre, a commercial gas cylinder is ₹600, and the cost of a crate has gone from ₹250 to ₹360. The overall production cost has increased by at least 40%,” he said.

Bamul president D.K. Suresh said that a slight downward revision in curd prices is expected post Deepavali. “We have to follow the instructions of the government to reduce the price of curd. It will be reduced after Deepavali, after holding a meeting with the presidents of milk unions across the State. Revised prices will be released soon,” he said. The price of one litre of curd is ₹68 per litre now.

articles.title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies
China denied on Monday (November 9, 2026) there was a spy plot attempt to ensnare Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the spying allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.

Mr. Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.
“The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft.
Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) that the company would launch an investigation into the case. Mr. Huang did not name the person in the extramarital affair.

China had previously denied the New York Times report that said Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that faced claims of smuggling advanced chips into China, and that she was a spy for Beijing.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.

Mr. Huang had pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China in recent years, successfully lobbying U.S. President Donald Trump to allow his company to sell H200 chips this year. However, it is uncertain if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy these chips en masse.

While those chips are not Nvidia's most cutting-edge models, they are still advanced. Previously, Mr. Huang also lobbied Mr. Trump to sell the less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed for the Chinese market while complying with U.S. export restrictions.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilising U.S.-China relations.
“Whenever China-U.S. relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows,” the state-owned Global Times said.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilising U.S.-China relations.

articles.title: Untangling Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s Chinese spy connection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia said that it was investigating its Mr. Huang after he told the board he had been intimate with a customer, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy, per a report by New York Times

Nvidia is the world leader in making chips for AI data centres, and its role in providing the critical hardware for the development of large language models cannot be understated. Powerful AI tools like Anthropic’s Claude, Google’s Gemini, Meta’s Muse, and OpenAI’s GPT exist today because of Nvidia’s graphic processing unit (GPU) chips. So, it is only fair to say that if AI is the solar system, Nvidia is the sun powering American tech companies, plus those in China building competing AI models, that orbit around it. Accessing Nvidia’s GPUs to build powerful AI models started becoming difficult for Chinese companies as Washington began tightening controls on who can buy the chipmaker’s advanced processors.

articles.title: World entering ‘age of climate extremes’: UN chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The UN chief statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organization released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels

The world is entering a new reality where climate extremes are the norm, the United Nations chief Antonio Guterres warned on Monday (November 9, 2026), urging leaders at the COP31 climate conference in Turkiye to “get serious”.
“A supersized El Nino is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change,” the UN secretary general said in a statement.

As leaders gathered in Antalya for the UN climate summit, Mr. Guterres called on them to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”.
His statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organization released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels.
Each of the past 12 years have been among the hottest 12 years on record, the agency said, with this year expected to be among the hottest ever.

“What we are seeing gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva, cautioning that the current exceptionally strong El Nino could unleash more heat and extreme weather well into next year.
“We should prepare for another record-breaking year in 2027.”
The global average surface temperature between January and September this year was around 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average, the WMO said.
And this year’s El Nino — expected to be the strongest since 1950 at least — could push the figure higher by the end of the year.

Preliminary data shows 2026 figuring among the four hottest years on record, WMO climate information chief John Kenned told reporters, adding though that “with the El Nina developing, we might see when the final numbers come in that we’re close to the top”.
The naturally occurring weather phenomenon releases heat from the ocean, which this year has been the warmest ever measured, Saulo pointed out.
El Nino is declared when the sea surface temperature is half a degree above average in the tropical Pacific, but from now through January, WMO forecasts “it may be 3.8C above average”, she said.

articles.title: The worm that broke the internet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Even before the World Wide Web came into existence, there was Morris worm — one of the first computer worms that the internet ever saw. Created by Robert Tappan Morris, then a student, it changed the landscape of networking like never before. A.S.Ganesh wriggles his way through this story to hand you the best bits…

It is the dream of every (or most) digital native, or all of us living through the Information Age, to break the internet. For the uninitiated, that’s the process of posting or publishing something on the internet that goes on to create a terrific amount of interest, shock, or excitement. When you break the internet, a large number of people usually end up sharing or reacting to your initial post.

Even as you continue to think about your next post, picture, or reel that can maybe achieve this, spare a moment to think about whether the internet has ever been broken. Turns out, the answer is a resounding yes. But no, it wasn’t a celebrity posting about their latest life update, creating ripples across the globe. It was, in fact, the result of a student unleashing a computer worm in an experiment gone wrong.
Science, Space & Environment Report: The worm that broke the internet. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: How governmentality exacerbates the problem of farmers’ stubble burning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A new study by researchers Sujit Raghunathrao Jagadale and Javed M. Shaikh at the Indian Institute of Management, Amritsar analyses the problem of stubble burning from the lens of ‘governmentality’ and market failure

Jagadale, S. R., and, Shaikh, J. M, ‘Governmentality and Marketing System Failure: The Case of Stubble Burning and Climate Change in Neoliberal India’, Journal of Macromarketing , 2025 https://doi.org/10.1177/02761467251318608

C ome November, the Indo-Gangetic Plain is often clouded in a pall of pollution. The cessation of monsoon winds from the preceding four months and a drop in temperatures lead to pollutants from year-round sources, such as vehicles, power plants, construction dust and other suspended particulate matter, persisting as a black shroud because of the formation of an ‘inversion layer’. This means that these particles aren’t ‘flushed out’ from the region by the stronger winds at the higher atmospheric reaches. Add to this the contribution of stubble burning. Particulate matter from the burning of farm stubble — rice chaff — by farmers in Punjab, and to a smaller extent Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh — is added to this haze, worsening the already noxious air quality in Delhi and several other north Indian cities. Farm stubble is burnt in October and November because it is the cheapest method employed by farmers to prepare their soil for Rabi wheat.

articles.title: At 1,152, Punjab records season’s biggest single-day jump in farm fires on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice
Punjab witnessed its sharpest single-day spike in paddy stubble-burning incidents this season on Deepavali, with 1,152 farm fires reported across the State, according to official data.
This pushed the State's total count from 3,307 on November 7 to 4,459 on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The highest number of farm fires this season has been reported from Tarn Taran at 654, the data showed.
The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice.
The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1.

With 194 fires, Sangrur recorded the highest number of stubble-burning incidents on Sunday (November 8), taking its seasonal tally to 488. Ferozepur reported 157 incidents, bringing its total to 592; and Bathinda added 132 cases, taking its count to 406.
Patiala recorded 92 fresh farm fires, raising its cumulative tally to 288. Barnala reported 91 new incidents and Ludhiana 71.

The data showed that till Sunday (November 8), enforcement agencies had registered 884 FIRs under Section 223 (disobedience of orders promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and marked 1,017 red entries in land revenue records against farmers found burning stubble.
Fines totalling over ₹62 lakh have been imposed as environmental compensation in 1,228 cases of stubble burning, with over ₹32 lakh already recovered.

Recently, taking a serious view of the "very high" number of farm fires in Punjab, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) held a meeting with senior bureaucrats and police officers from 12 districts to review steps to prevent stubble burning.
The CAQM directed that the monitoring and enforcement drive must be intensified and nodal officers must be held accountable for lack of monitoring and for failure to prevent farm fires.

articles.title: Number of villages without 4G connectivity falls by three-fourths in four years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Data obtained by The Hindu under the Right to Information Act shows a sharp decline in the number of villages without serviceable internet speeds

The number of villages without 4G connectivity has fallen from 45,180 in 2022 to 11,372, about a fourth of the earlier figure, according to data from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) obtained by The Hindu under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The reduction is partly the result of BSNL’s 4G saturation project. But the figure is beyond the scheme’s initial target of covering 24,680 villages, indicating complementary efforts by private operators.

The reduction is notable because of historical gaps in connectivity between urban and rural India. The country is still far from universal smartphone ownership, even as cities and towns often enjoy extensive high-speed 5G coverage and affordable wired home broadband. The development also comes at a time when additions to wired broadband subscriptions have stagnated for months, making mobile broadband — the primary means of internet access for Indians — all the more important.

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali night, data goes missing at several govt monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “When the hourly PM2.5 data is missing, it will artificially lower the Air Quality Index (AQI), showing better air quality, when the actual air quality is worse,” Manoj Kumar, analyst, Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) said

At the peak of pollution, following the bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali night, air quality data was missing from several monitoring stations managed by government authorities, raising questions over the actual air pollution levels.

Air quality readings went blank for several stations for many hours, as per websites of the Delhi government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) and the Central government’s Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
Data of PM2.5 was missing for several hours for many stations in Delhi including Anand Vihar, Patparganj, Bawana, among others, as per DPCC’s website.
PM2.5 (Particulate matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.
Last year also, data went missing from many stations in a similar way during Deepavali.

Manoj Kumar, analyst, Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finland-based non-profit research organisation, said that missing hourly PM2.5 data “raises concerns” over Delhi’s air quality assessment.

“Since midnight on November 8 until 5 a.m. on November 9, 227 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation,” Mr. Kumar said.
“When the hourly PM2.5 data is missing, it will artificially lower the Air Quality Index (AQI), showing better air quality, when the actual air quality is worse,” he added.

When asked about air quality data in Delhi missing in several monitoring stations, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra told the media that the government will look into the issue within an hour and inform the media about it.

Before the data went missing for two hours, the level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Patparganj was 2,597 micrograms per cubic metre at 1 a.m. on Monday (November 9, 2026) - about 173.13 times the WHO permissible limit - of 15 micrograms per cubic metre for a 24-hour period.
Similarly, after data went missing for three hours, the level of PM2.5 in Anand Vihar was 1,396 micrograms per cubic metre at 3 a.m. on Monday — about 93.06 times the WHO permissible limit.
Meanwhile, in the CPCB website, the data for PM2.5 seemed to be capped at 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre, showing more gaps in data than the DPCC website.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi dares PM to debate him on who is ‘anti-national’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Accusing the PM of branding his political opponents as ‘Naxals’ following his Deepavali speech to CRPF personnel, the Congress leader reiterates his challenge to debate him on ‘who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces’

A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi cautioned Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel to be alert about “ dimagi [intellectual] Naxals ”, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday (November 9, 2026) dared the Prime Minister to debate him on who was an anti-national.

In a post on social media platform X addressed to CRPF personnel, Mr. Gandhi said their expressions showed they had not been convinced by the Prime Minister’s remarks. “Your faces said it all: you didn’t buy the PM’s lies,” he said.
Accusing Mr. Modi of branding his political opponents as “Naxals”, Mr. Gandhi reiterated his challenge to debate him on “who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces”.

“He called us Naxals. My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place. My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won’t have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again,” the Congress leader said.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), addressing security personnel at a CRPF camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, during his Deepavali visit, Mr. Modi said that while armed Maoists had been eliminated, “ dimagi Naxals” had infiltrated political parties and organisations, and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy. He called for identifying and defeating such elements.

The Prime Minister had also used the term in his Independence Day address in August, arguing that ideological supporters of Naxalism continued to pose a challenge despite success in eliminating armed insurgency.
The Congress accused Mr. Modi of being “distraught, disturbed and desperate”, adding that his “jhola (bag)-picking-up time” was approaching.

“The Prime Minister has not spared the country his usual abusive language even on Diwali. Once again, he has called some of his political opponents ‘intellectual Naxals’. Most objectionable is that he abused an extremely solemn and non-political occasion for this, wore the uniform of the security forces, and hurled a barrage of mud at his political opponents. This is an open assault on all norms of propriety and tradition. But when have these gentlemen ever cared about principles and ideals?” Congress’s communications chief Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X on Sunday.

Mr. Gandhi has repeatedly challenged Mr. Modi to an open debate, claiming that he could establish within five minutes that the Prime Minister was a “traitor”. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders have dismissed the challenge, accusing the Congress leader of avoiding debates in Parliament.

Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that Parliament was already an available forum for debate and asked Mr. Gandhi to show “some seriousness and responsibility” in discharging his role as the Leader of the Opposition.

articles.title: Andhra SCPCR to organise meeting on ‘Making Father’s Name Optional’ with stakeholders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: SCPCR, in association with NGOs, Children of India Foundation and HELP, will conduct the meeting

The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (AP SCPCR) will organise a State-level consultation on ‘Making Father’s Name not Mandatory in Official Documents’, with NGOs and child rights bodies.

SCPCR, in association with NGOs, Children of India Foundation and HELP, will conduct the meeting at Hotel Swarna Palace, from 10 a.m. onwards on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), said Commission Chairman Vetukuri A.V.S. Suryanarayana Raju.

Chairpersons of Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs), Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), Central Administrators of One Stop Centres (OSCs), Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) and Juvenile Police Units of Krishna, NTR, Palnadu, Guntur, Eluru and West Godavari districts, and child rights bodies will attend the day-long meeting, the SCPCR Chairman said.

articles.title: Police rush to Belagavi City Corporation after bomb threat, declared hoax
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police began the search from inside the meeting hall to officers chambers, various departments, rooms, toilets and the vehicles in the parking area. But no explosive materials were found even after one hour of search.

Police rushed to the Belagavi City Corporation (BCC) after a staff member received a call about a bomb placed in the office in Belagavi on Monday (November 9, 2026). Officers later said that it was a hoax.
The call, however, spread panic among the staff and officers who ran outside to safety.

City police commissioner Prakash Nikam rushed a team of jurisdictional officers and members of the dog squad to the BCC office and began an inspection. Police inspector J.M. Kalimirchi and others also rushed to the spot.

Police arrived with metal detectors, and other equipment. They began the search from inside the meeting hall to officers chambers, various departments, rooms, toilets and the vehicles in the parking area. However, no explosive materials were found even after one hour of search.

articles.title: Pakistani TV anchorperson shot dead at home in Rawalpindi; husband held
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A Pakistani anchorperson was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi, with police taking her husband into custody and seizing the suspected weapon.

Rabia Ahsan, who worked as an anchor and programme host with a local private TV channel, was found dead at her home in the Gulshanabad area of the city on Sunday (November 8, 2026), the Dawn newspaper reported.
City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera said Ahsan's husband had been taken into custody and the suspected weapon seized. An investigation has been launched, he added.
Mr. Sukhera, along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations and the SSP investigations, visited the crime scene with a team of forensic experts.
According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that the victim's husband had claimed that the gunshot was fired accidentally.
Mr. Sukhera said teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) were collecting evidence from the scene, while the body was being taken to a hospital for postmortem examination.
A case was being registered and an investigation would be conducted on merit, he said.
Meanwhile, First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness over the killing and strongly condemned the violence.
She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable, a statement issued by the Presidency said.
Ms. Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concern over what she described as a “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.

She recalled the murder of Hina Javed, a 45-year-old digital media executive who was found dead at her Rawalpindi residence in August with signs of torture, and noted that the outcome of the investigation into the case was still awaited.

articles.title: 2026 to be one of four warmest years on record: World Meteorological Organization
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate, said WMO

The year 2026 will be one of the four warmest years on record, with the global average temperature for January-September 2026 touching 1.47 degrees Celsius higher than pre-industrial times (the average of the 1850-1900 period), according to a new World Meteorological Organization report.
It added that this global average temperature figure was higher than the full-year averages in 2025 and 2023, and only slightly lower than 2024, which is the warmest year on record.

Moreover, the figure is likely to rise through the end of 2026 because of the warming effect of the prevailing El Nino, which has been intensifying since August and is expected to be the strongest on record by December.

The report, ‘State of the Climate Report’, was released by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Friday – the first day of this year’s UN climate meeting, known as COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye.

In a statement, WMO Secretary General Celeste Saulo said, “The past four years have been the warmest in the 177-year observational record, and the heat in the oceans is breaking records for the tenth year in a row.”
“The ongoing El Nino is forecast to be one of the strongest on record, and the heat it releases from the ocean will continue to fuel high temperatures and extreme weather into 2027,” she added.
The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate.

The imbalance reached its highest level since monitoring began, as greenhouse gases trap unprecedented amounts of heat and upset the equilibrium between incoming energy from the sun and outgoing energy, according to the WMO report.

It revealed that the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide has increased by 53% from around 278 parts per million (ppm) in 1750 to about 426.8 ppm in 2025. Global averaged methane concentrations increased from 729 parts per billion (ppb) in 1750 by 167% to 1,948 ppb in 2025.
Moreover, the ocean absorbs 90% of the excess heat, and 2026 is on track to be the tenth successive year of record ocean warmth, the report said.
It also highlighted that extreme events impacted lives and livelihoods, undermined food security, deepened poverty, and contributed to displacement across multiple regions.
For instance, the European heatwaves, drought and wildfires led to more than 30,000 excess deaths, according to preliminary estimates.

articles.title: Kremlin hopes U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.
But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
He also praised the “successful humanitarian peace-building efforts” by first lady Melania Trump, adding that “we hope that all of this will continue.”
Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.
Mr. Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Mr. Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an “internal matter” for the U.S.
In recent months, Mr. Trump's actions appeared to favour Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Mr. Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Mr. Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

At the same time, Ukraine reported a throttling of Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX. Mr. Trump denied being behind the brief slowing of Starshield, but the move to limit the system that serves as the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and battlefield communications was widely seen as part of Washington's efforts to pressure Kyiv.

The diesel deal appeared to falter this week after U.S. federal and state officials warned that handling any shipments could bring legal consequences, and two U.S.-bound tankers changed course. The Kremlin sought to play down the development, saying deliveries will continue.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Firecracker smoke releases fine particles and harmful gases that irritate the airways and affect lung health. Experts explain the short- and long-term effects of exposure and whether the damage persists after air quality improves

A few hours of exposure to firecracker smoke can be enough to trigger coughing, wheezing or breathlessness, particularly in people living with asthma or other respiratory conditions. The effects, however, are not limited to those with an existing diagnosis. High concentrations of particulate matter and gases can irritate the airways in anyone.

The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a numerical measure that converts the levels of different air pollutants into a single figure to indicate how polluted the air is and the likely health effects. India’s Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) calculates it using eight pollutants, including PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide.

articles.title: Chennai sees dozens of cracker-related eye injuries; doctors call for caution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The day may have been wet, but Chennaiites still went all out to bring in light and sparkles on Deepavali day, which fell on Sunday (November 8, 2026). While awareness about safety has increased, ophthalmologists in the city have once again called for caution and reiterated protective measures, as they have received dozens of cases of cracker-related injuries.
The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital received around 50 cases, with about 10 cases having to be admitted, a senior official said.

The emergency clinic at Sankara Nethralaya, over the Diwali weekend, saw 45 cases of firecracker injuries at its main campus. Two underwent wound repair surgery, while two others are scheduled for surgery on Monday, November 9, according to T.S. Surendran, its chairman.
Chennai’s air quality deteriorates to ‘poor’ the morning after Deepavali
Poor response from residents to Chennai Corporation’s appeal for segregated collection of cracker waste

At Dr. Agarwals Eye Hospital, nearly 20 patients came in with cracker-related injuries, said S. Soundari, regional head, clinical services. One of these, she explained, was a very serious case that had been taken up for surgery. Another patient lit a firecracker, but it did not blast. He went near it to take a look, and it blasted in his face, injuring both eyes. The remaining injuries were mostly small, and would be treated medically, she said. Four cases involved children; the rest were adults, mostly in their 30s and 40s.

At Rajan Eye Care, about 15 patients have been seen over the past three days or so, said Mohan Rajan, chairman and medical director of the hospital. One patient had to undergo a surgery, while minor injuries were treated as outpatients.

Doctors have reiterated caution. Dr. Soundari called for wearing protective eye gear while bursting firecrackers, supervising children properly, and importantly, not trying to touch the eye or take objects out by oneself. “Come to a doctor immediately if there is an eye injury,” she stressed. Dr. Rajan noted that bystanders often got hurt and should be careful to maintain an adequate distance..

articles.title: Cyber bullying affects one in ten students worldwide; AI fuels new threat: UNESCO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The United Nations agency has called upon countries to invest in digital safety measures, teacher preparation, and mental health support for students, in coordination with technology companies

One in three students across the globe experiences bullying every month, while one in 10 faces cyber bullying, the UNESCO said, warning that AI is accelerating new forms of technology-facilitated violence (TFV).

UNESCO's new policy brief, ‘Connected and Safe’, shows that nudification apps, voice cloning, automated harassment and AI companion apps used for grooming are now surfacing in school-based incidents across multiple regions.
The United Nations agency has called upon countries to invest in digital safety measures, teacher preparation, and mental health support for students, in coordination with technology companies.

According to Khaled El-Enany, director-general of UNESCO, one in three learners experience bullying every month, while one in ten face cyber bullying. Behind these figures are millions of children whose education, health and well-being are at risk, with consequences that can extend far beyond the classroom.

"Online and technology-facilitated violence (TFV) is no longer a peripheral concern for education systems. It is part of the reality of school life for many learners, with direct consequences for safety, well-being, participation and learning. Around one in ten learners worldwide has experienced cyber bullying, and across 44 countries in Europe, Central Asia and North America, prevalence rose from 12 to 15 per cent between 2018 and 2022, among both boys and girls," the policy brief said.

"Some learners are more exposed than others. Girls, learners with disabilities, learners of diverse sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics, and those marginalised by socio-economic status or geography face distinct and often more severe forms of harm," it said.
In the context of bullying, data shows that girls are just as likely as boys to experience bullying, although the types of bullying differ.

"Physical sexual violence (assault, harassment and rape) can affect both boys and girls, but girls are more likely to experience this form of violence. Corporal punishment and all forms of violent discipline are also influenced by gender, with boys more likely to experience physical corporal punishment than girls and learners likely to be punished to reinforce expectations regarding behaviours deemed socially appropriate for each gender," the brief said.

UNESCO argued that responsibility for safer digital environments for students must be shared between governments, technology companies, platforms and regulators, as schools alone cannot face this issue.

"Safer schools require sustained investment in teacher preparation, mental health and psychosocial support, reporting and response systems, digital safety measures, and coordinated action across education, child protection, health and technology sectors.

"UNESCO recently launched the process towards a new global recommendation on young people and digital environments in the age of AI, to ensure that these technologies protect children's rights and well-being, strengthen critical thinking and empower them to shape their own future," it said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 09 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Cyber bullying affects one in ten students worldwide; AI fuels new threat: UNESCO

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

The United Nations agency has called upon countries to invest in digital safety measures, teacher preparation, and mental health support for students, in coordination with technology companies

One in three students across the globe experiences bullying every month, while one in 10 faces cyber bullying, the UNESCO said, warning that AI is accelerating new forms of technology-facilitated violence (TFV).

UNESCO's new policy brief, ‘Connected and Safe’, shows that nudification apps, voice cloning, automated harassment and AI companion apps used for grooming are now surfacing in school-based incidents across multiple regions.

The United Nations agency has called upon countries to invest in digital safety measures, teacher preparation, and mental health support for students, in coordination with technology companies.

According to Khaled El-Enany, director-general of UNESCO, one in three learners experience bullying every month, while one in ten face cyber bullying. Behind these figures are millions of children whose education, health and well-being are at risk, with consequences that can extend far beyond the classroom.

"Online and technology-facilitated violence (TFV) is no longer a peripheral concern for education systems. It is part of the reality of school life for many learners, with direct consequences for safety, well-being, participation and learning. Around one in ten learners worldwide has experienced cyber bullying, and across 44 countries in Europe, Central Asia and North America, prevalence rose from 12 to 15 per cent between 2018 and 2022, among both boys and girls," the policy brief said.

"Some learners are more exposed than others. Girls, learners with disabilities, learners of diverse sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics, and those marginalised by socio-economic status or geography face distinct and often more severe forms of harm," it said.

In the context of bullying, data shows that girls are just as likely as boys to experience bullying, although the types of bullying differ.

"Physical sexual violence (assault, harassment and rape) can affect both boys and girls, but girls are more likely to experience this form of violence. Corporal punishment and all forms of violent discipline are also influenced by gender, with boys more likely to experience physical corporal punishment than girls and learners likely to be punished to reinforce expectations regarding behaviours deemed socially appropriate for each gender," the brief said.

UNESCO argued that responsibility for safer digital environments for students must be shared between governments, technology companies, platforms and regulators, as schools alone cannot face this issue.

"Safer schools require sustained investment in teacher preparation, mental health and psychosocial support, reporting and response systems, digital safety measures, and coordinated action across education, child protection, health and technology sectors.

"UNESCO recently launched the process towards a new global recommendation on young people and digital environments in the age of AI, to ensure that these technologies protect children's rights and well-being, strengthen critical thinking and empower them to shape their own future," it said.

articles.title: Belagavi Police arrest woman, six accused for murdering her son
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The body was found in a drain on Kolhapur Road last week
Belagavi Police have arrested seven people, including a 44-year-old woman, on the charge of killing the woman’s 24-year-old son.
Meena Narayana, a resident of R.T. Nagar in Bengaluru, her 34-year-old friend Rakesh Parashurama Jamuni of Ichalkaranji in Maharashtra and his five associates have been arrested.
The names of four of Jamuni’s associates were given as Sachin Kamble, Manoj Kamble, Tammanna Kamble and Eknath Kamble. The other accused is a child in conflict with law.
The seven accused eliminated Meena’s son Vijaya Narayana after he objected to his widowed mother’s relationship with Jamuni, the police said.
The body was found in a drain on Kolhapur Road last week.
Investigators found strangulation marks on Vijaya Narayana’s neck and registered a murder case.
Meena visited the police station and identified the body found in the drain as that of her son Vijaya Narayana on Wednesday last.
The accused is said to have drugged the victim with a drink and killed him in Belagavi on November 1. They dumped the body in the drain and fled, the police said.

articles.title: KMC Commissioner directs officials to identify dumping spots, boost awareness on waste disposal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inspecting sanitation operations across Kurnool, KMC Commissioner emphasises waste collection must continue without interruption, even on public holidays

Kurnool Municipal Corporation (KMC) Commissioner Challa Obulesu has directed officials to identify roads, vacant plots, and other public spaces where garbage is being dumped and to create awareness among the residents to discourage indiscriminate dumping. The KMC Commissioner also instructed officials to ensure public cooperation with the door-to-door waste collection system.

Mr. Obulesu inspected the sanitation operations in Gibson Colony, Birla Gate, Krishna Nagar, and Chennamma Circle on Monday. Subsequently, at the Kalluru ward office, he examined the equipment recently procured for water supply and repair works.

During an inspection of the Anna Canteen at the government hospital, the sanitation supervisory staff brought to the Commissioner’s attention the challenges they faced regarding waste collection. Responding immediately, the Commissioner consulted with the sanitation staff and issued orders to ensure that waste was collected from the hospital twice daily.
He emphasised that waste collection must continue without interruption, even on public holidays.

articles.title: Sabarimala ghee supply in a bind; TDB opens talks with Milma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As the Travancore Devaswom Board had invited bids for 50,000 litres of ghee but failed to find eligible suppliers, it has been holding discussions with office-bearers of the Milma Thiruvananthapuram Regional Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union to plug the gap in supply

With the Mandala-Makaravilakku season in Sabarimala barely a week away, the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) is turning to Milma once again to plug the gap in ghee supply after two rounds of tendering failed to find eligible bidders.

The board had invited bids for 50,000 litres of ghee but failed to find eligible suppliers. Though Milma did not participate in the tender, the TDB has been holding discussions with office-bearers of the Milma Thiruvananthapuram Regional Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union.
TDB president K. Jayakumar said the board was yet to take a final call on procuring ghee from Milma for Aravana production and would seek legal advice before deciding on the matter.

According to him, the anticipated shortfall at the beginning of the season was only around 10,000 litres and there was no immediate cause for concern over availability. Ghee supplies were expected to increase once the temple opens on November 16, though the shortfall could affect production until then. Preparations for Aravana production are progressing, with the board currently holding a stock of 30 lakh tins. Arrangements are being finalised to produce 3.5 lakh tins daily.
“We are planning to produce another 30 lakh tins in the coming days. Appam production will also begin in a time-bound manner,” Mr. Jayakumar said.

Milma’s possible return as a supplier comes amid an ongoing Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) probe into the supply of spurious ghee to the Sannidhanam in its name last season. The investigation found that the contractor entrusted with transporting the ghee had diverted around 11,000 kg of Milma ghee meant for Sabarimala and replaced it with a cheaper product.

Meanwhile, the deadline for completing construction and other preparatory works, including maintenance, ahead of the season expires on Tuesday. Despite the TDB’s claims that preparations are complete, sources said several works at the Sannidhanam and Nilackal, including road reconstruction, remain unfinished and could take another week to complete.

articles.title: Manipur Census to remain on hold until April 2027, says High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 30, the Centre issued a notification excluding the State from the nationwide headcount ‘till further declaration’

The High Court of Manipur has said that the Census in the State will remain suspended until at least April 30, 2027, while the Centre considers requests from campaign groups and residents to delay or change the dates for the exercise.

A Bench of Chief Justice M. Sundar and Justice A. Guneshwar Sharma said postponement notices already issued by the Centre and the State government must remain in force until the date specified and cannot be withdrawn or altered.

The court’s November 4 order disposed of two petitions, one filed by Imphal resident Shanta Singh Nahakpam and the other by the Kangleipak Students’ Association and the International Peace and Social Advancement. They had challenged the plan to begin house-listing, the first stage of the 2027 Census, in the State from September 1.

The petitioners argued that conditions in Manipur, where thousands of people have been displaced by the ethnic violence that began in May 2023, were not right for an accurate headcount. They also expressed fears that Census figures could affect the redrawing of Assembly constituency boundaries.

The court noted that some groups wanted the National Register of Citizens (NRC) to be updated before the Census operation is undertaken and the 2001 Census figures in certain hill areas to be recounted.

The court asked the Registrar General of India and the Census Commissioner to consider the demands raised in existing petitions on their “own merits” and issue a detailed, reasoned decision. It said the petitioners and anyone else could send additional petitions by November 25.

The court said the authorities concerned may hold public consultations after the decisions by April 30, 2027. “If it (public consultation) is considered not necessary, the reasons shall be set out in the common speaking order,” it said.
The court further said the Census would remain on hold for four weeks after the decision was issued, allowing anyone dissatisfied with it to approach the court again.
On August 31, the Centre told the court that it would postpone house-listing in Manipur, and the State government agreed to put its schedule on hold.

The Centre issued a notification on September 5, deferring the exercise in the State. Another notification, issued on October 30, said the population enumeration would be held from late January to the end of February 2027, with midnight of March 1, 2027, as the reference date.
The October 30 notification also said Manipur had been excluded from the nationwide headcount “till further declaration”.
Meitei and Naga organisations want the citizens’ register updated before the Census, but the pro-Census Kuki-Zo organisations see the NRC demand as “premature and unjustified”.

The court asked the Registrar General of India and the Census Commissioner to consider the demands raised in existing petitions on their “own merits” and issue a detailed, reasoned decision. It said the petitioners and anyone else could send additional petitions by November 25.

The court said the authorities concerned may hold public consultations after the decisions by April 30, 2027. “If it (public consultation) is considered not necessary, the reasons shall be set out in the common speaking order,” it said.

The court further said the Census would remain on hold for four weeks after the decision was issued, allowing anyone dissatisfied with it to approach the court again.

On August 31, the Centre told the court that it would postpone house-listing in Manipur, and the State government agreed to put its schedule on hold.

The Centre issued a notification on September 5, deferring the exercise in the State. Another notification, issued on October 30, said the population enumeration would be held from late January to the end of February 2027, with midnight of March 1, 2027, as the reference date.

The October 30 notification also said Manipur had been excluded from the nationwide headcount “till further declaration”.

Meitei and Naga organisations want the citizens’ register updated before the Census, but the pro-Census Kuki-Zo organisations see the NRC demand as “premature and unjustified”.

1. Core Context & Background: On October 30, the Centre issued a notification excluding the State from the nationwide headcount ‘till further declaration’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The High Court of Manipur has said that the Census in the State will remain suspended until at least April 30, 2027, while the Centre considers requests from campaign groups and residents to delay or change the dates for the exercise.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Meitei and Naga organisations want the citizens’ register updated before the Census, but the pro-Census Kuki-Zo organisations see the NRC demand as “premature and unjustified”.

articles.title: Vinodkumar Kallolickal takes charge as KCHR chairperson
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vinodkumar Kallolickal, currently Professor at the Department of History, Maharaja’s College, Ernakulam, has taken charge as the Chairperson of the Kerala Council for Historical Research (KCHR).
Prof. Kallolickal succeeds K.N. Ganesh as chairperson, KCHR.
The State government had issued an order regarding the appointment on November 7.

A resident of Vennala, ernakulam, Prof. Kallolickal has a PhD from the Aligarh Muslim University and a post-doctoral fellowship from the Transdisciplinary University, Bengaluru. He has written and edited 21 books in Malayalam and English and has several papers to his name in research publications.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Deadlines to the two rounds were last extended in September by about two months to November 15.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday (November 7, 2026) that President Donald Trump launched the war against Iran, even if it was not “necessarily popular”, to safeguard the world from the country's nuclear ambitions.

He would not comment directly about the Republican wipeout in Tuesday's (November 3) elections, which delivered a resounding rebuke to Mr. Trump. The unpopularity of the Iran war and its impact on gasoline prices and other parts of the economy helped Democrats seize control of Congress.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Marco Rubio: Iran can never be allowed to become a nuclear weapons power

Asked about Vice-President J.D. Vance's social media post last week that largely blamed the war for the Republican losses, Mr. Rubio told reporters that Mr. Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and worked to stop the Islamic Republic from pursuing a nuclear weapon.
Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war

“He addressed it even though oftentimes the right thing to do for the country — confronting difficult challenges for the security of our country — doing it isn't necessarily popular, but necessary,” Mr. Rubio said in Florida before heading to a Group of 7 Foreign Ministers meeting in Paris.

America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway where one-fifth of the world's oil transited before the war.
“I can tell you, this historically — for history — will go down as one of the best things we ever did," Mr. Trump said. "Because if they ever had a nuclear weapon, they would blow up the world."

Iran has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kg of uranium that is enriched up to 60% purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90%.
With no clear administration strategy to wind down the conflict and West Asia on edge over the possibility of a return to major hostilities, mediators are trying to revive talks between the sides.
Mr. Rubio said, “I wouldn't say we're at the verge of a breakthrough.”

He reiterated that Mr. Trump prefers a diplomatic solution, but “right now, it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic.”

articles.title: Trump says likely to meet Putin, Xi at China APEC summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda

United States President Donald Trump has said he will likely meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in a rare trilateral leaders’ meeting on the sidelines of the APEC gathering in Shenzhen next week.

Beijing said on Monday (November 9, 2026) it was “in communication with relevant parties” over the meeting, not ruling out the possibility as leaders gather for the APEC summit in southern China on November 18 and 19.

Mr. Trump on Sunday (November 8, 2026) indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda. “One of the meetings will be with President Putin and President Xi, and that’ll be interesting. We’re talking ​a lot of things, including denuclearisation, but we’ll ​be talking a lot of things. We’re trying to end the ‌war ⁠in Iran,” Mr. Trump was quoted as saying.

Asked about his remarks, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday (November 9, 2026) did not rule out the prospect of a meeting, saying that China was in communication with relevant parties regarding the meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. Presidents.

Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi will meet bilaterally next week for the third time this year, following the U.S. President’s visit to Beijing in May and the Chinese President travelling to Washington in September . They will meet once again at the end of the year at the G20 in Miami, marking an unusual four meetings in a year.

Both countries have sought to inject more stability in relations and pursue what they call “a constructive relationship of strategic stability”, even as they have exchanged blows on issues including trade tariffs, restrictions on semiconductors, rare earths and Taiwan.

Chinese analysts have sought to play down the significance of a possible trilateral summit, just as they also played down Mr. Trump’s remarks in Beijing earlier this year of a “G2”. Russia was “most enthusiastic” among the three, Su Liuqiang, a scholar at the Centre for American Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said in an interview with state media, adding that an informal exchange was likelier than a more structured, formal trilateral summit.

“On the one hand, there is substantial political resistance in the U.S. Anti-Russia sentiment remains strong in both the U.S. and among its European allies, with opposition to negotiating with Moscow while bypassing Ukraine and Europe. On the other hand, the three countries have differing priorities. Russia’s core concern is negotiations on a ceasefire in Ukraine, the U.S. is interested in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and non-proliferation, China supports peace talks but must also balance its relations with the U.S., Russia, Europe and Ukraine. In this context, a low-profile trilateral meeting is the more realistic option,” he said, adding that practical outcomes could emphasise stabilising global energy supplies.

While China preferred “multilateralism” over ideas such as the G2 or a U.S.-China-Russia triumvirate, Mr. Su said a meeting would still be significant in suggesting that while structural competition between big powers would still continue to define global geopolitics, there was increasing interest in “managing that competition and preventing it from escalating or spinning out of control”.

articles.title: Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia

U.S. President Donald Trump will meet ‌the Prime Minister of key mediator Qatar on Monday (November 9, 2026) as efforts to end the ​Iran war ramp up following last week's midterm elections, though senior U.S. and Gulf ⁠officials cast doubt on the chances of an imminent deal.

With no victory in sight more than eight months into the conflict he launched alongside Israel on February 28, Mr. Trump has played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon, but remains ‌unwilling to accept an existing Iranian truce plan.

Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia.

Sheikh Mohammed ‌bin ⁠Abdulrahman Al-Thani, who is both Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, will meet Mr. ⁠Trump and Vice President J. D. Vance in Washington later on Monday (November 9, 2026) after having visited Tehran last week.

Iran's proposal to end the war involves an end to the U.S. blockade of its ports, the lifting of some sanctions, and a halt to bombing in return for ​Tehran stopping its own blockade of the Strait ‌of Hormuz, with talks on its nuclear programme and other sanctions to follow.

The U.S. has repeatedly rejected that plan, which Iran has said could be condensed to a two-day timeframe, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sunday (November 8, 2026) describing Tehran's conditions as "outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic".
Iran's Foreign Ministry ‌spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei defended the plan on Monday (November 9, 2026) as the most reasonable offer on the table.

Senior ​U.S. Republicans including Mr. Vance have blamed their party's dire showing in last week's elections on the Iran war, but despite growing domestic political pressure to end the conflict, Mr. Rubio said ⁠he did not believe a diplomatic breakthrough was imminent.
A senior United Arab Emirates official, Anwar Gargash, echoed that view on Monday (November 9, 2026), saying a comprehensive political settlement between the U.S. and Iran appeared difficult.
"We should... prepare for a ‌long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor stable regional order can be taken for granted," he said.

Mr. Vance, who led the negotiations for a short-lived truce in June, will also meet Mr. Al-Thani, whose country has been a prime mediator since early in the war, conveying messages between the sides and proposing ways to bridge their differences.

Sunday (November 8, 2026) night's strikes on Qeshm island did not impact vital infrastructure or services, a provincial official told Iran's semi-official Fars news agency on Monday (November 9, 2026). The U.S. has not commented on the Iranian ‌media reports.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: Man arrested after crashing car into park across from White House
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The driver of the vehicle was ‘quickly placed under arrest’ after he ‘became combative with law enforcement’, a U.S. Secret Service spokesperson said
The White House was briefly placed on lockdown on Monday (November 9, 2026) after a man crashed his car into the sidewalk of a park across from the presidential mansion.
The driver of the vehicle was "quickly placed under arrest" after he "became combative with law enforcement," a U.S. Secret Service spokesperson said.
Video taken by witnesses showed the man struggling with police after being pulled from his car, which crashed into a sign on the sidewalk of Lafayette Park across from the White House.
An explosive ordnance disposal team was called in to "sweep the vehicle as a precaution," the Secret Service spokesperson said in a statement.
Around the same time as the vehicle incident, "a second individual jumped a barricade near the northwest corner of Lafayette Park," the spokesperson said.
"That individual was also quickly placed under arrest," the spokesperson said. "Both incidents are under investigation."
The White House was locked down for around half an hour during the incidents, correspondents said.

articles.title: Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to more than a decade in prison
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”

British comedian and Hollywood star Russell Brand was sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault by the Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday (November 9, 2026). Brand, 51, was found guilty on Thursday (November 5, 2026) by the court of rape and three counts of sexual assault and not guilty on three other counts. He was charged in relation to a total of seven crimes. His crimes were committed between 2004 and 2009. The court found him guilty of raping a woman in 2009 at his home, after meeting her at a comedy show in the Hammersmith neighbourhood of London. Brand has the possibility of being released in about seven years subject to conditions, the judge said.

“The consequences of what happened have affected almost every aspect of my life. Even now, I continue to experience anxiety, difficulties with trust, reduced confidence and the lasting effects of trauma,” the woman who was raped said on Monday (November 9, 2026) at the sentencing.
One of his victims said she was in “shock and turmoil” and did not “have any respect” for herself as a result of the attack on her. The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”.

Brand had argued during the trial that while his past behaviour had been “wrong”, he had never forced himself on anybody. The actor was formerly a left-wing activist. In the early years of the current decade, he moved to the right, becoming skeptical of vaccines and the origins of COVID-19, building bonds with big names in U.S. President Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, including the President’s son, Donald Trump Jr., tech billionaire Elon Musk , commentators Alex Jones and Tucker Carlson, as well as Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the U.S. Health Secretary. In September, Brand participated in a video call event for the MAHA, Make America Healthy Again, movement, which is headed by Mr. Kennedy Jr. Brand converted to Christianity more recently and was baptized in the Thames in 2024.

U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday (November 8, 2026) cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN that it was "highly unlikely" so long as talks progressed.

articles.title: Dhaka wants Hasina extradited under prisoner exchange
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Hasina seeks fresh passport, but Minister Humayun Kabir calls ousted leader a “terrorist” and dismisses request; no response from MEA, sources say denial of passport may complicate matter if India were to extradite Hasina

Hours after a legal team representing deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport for her, the Government of Bangladesh asserted on Monday (November 9, 2026) that Ms. Hasina can return to Bangladesh through an “acceptable prisoner exchange” programme governed by the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
Speaking to the media in Dhaka, the country’s Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir described Ms. Hasina as a “terrorist” who had fled to India after committing crimes.

A source in Dhaka told The Hindu that Ms. Hasina has requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through a London-based legal firm, for a new passport and a National Identity Card. The official said the Ministry is verifying the letter and will take a final decision after internal consultations. Ms. Hasina’s passport was revoked soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising toppled her government.

“Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process,” said Mr. Kabir, in response to questions from journalists regarding the request.

He noted that Ms. Hasina is a convict sentenced to death and has no legal or moral right to obtain a passport. Mr. Kabir said India should hand over the ousted Prime Minister under the extradition treaty. He added that Ms. Hasina and several of her colleagues from the Awami League are responsible for violent crimes and financial fraud, and need to be brought to justice.

The Ministry of External Affairs is yet to respond to Mr. Kabir’s remarks, but a source familiar with the Indian stance on the matter told The Hindu that the Bangladeshi position of not issuing a passport to Ms. Hasina will further complicate the matter, as a passport will be needed if India were to consider her extradition.

The Bangladeshi official, who spoke to The Hindu , said over the phone, “We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London, seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the contents of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation.”

However, the Press Secretary of the Bangladesh High Commission, Md. Saidur Rahman, said the Bangladesh authorities are “not sure if the request is genuine”. “There is no way for us to verify whether the request was actually made on behalf of Sheikh Hasina, as the email sent by the law firm did not include any authorisation letter or supporting documents proving that the firm was authorised by her to make such a request,” he said.

articles.title: Twenty-one migrants die trying to reach Greece’s Crete: authorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, says Greek Coast Guard

Twenty-one people have died over the weekend trying to reach Greece’s island of Crete, a top destination for migrants headed for the European Union from Africa, authorities said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, the Greek coast guard said on Monday. Another body was later found on Monday afternoon.
Maritime police launched an emergency rescue late Saturday after a boat issued an alarm signal, with strong winds making sea conditions difficult, the coast guard said.
Around 28 survivors and one body, all Sudanese nationals, were picked up by another boat sailing nearby, then transferred to a police vessel and taken to Crete, authorities had said on Sunday.
Two Sudanese citizens, one of them 16, were arrested after being identified by the survivors as suspected people-smugglers, the authorities said.
During the night from Sunday to Monday, the coast guard found their boat, with seven additional bodies on board, it said.
In a separate incident, 12 bodies were found on a boat south of the island on Monday, while 18 people were rescued, the coast guard said.
In all, the Greek coast guard and the EU’s Frontex border agency rescued a total of 105 on Monday, according to the port authorities.
Crete has become one of the main entry points into the European Union for migrants departing from Libya and attempting the dangerous crossing to Greece.
Many of the attempted crossings turn deadly when the vessels sink or run into trouble.
According to the United Nations refugee agency, more than 37,000 migrants have arrived in Greece in 2026 so far.
Over 22,000 of those people landed on Crete, the country’s largest island.
